Surface: infra

## Current State

Reconcile classifies a pipeline run directory as `structurally-stuck` when it carries a skip reason of `no-worktree`, `no-branch`, `no-pr`, or `console-never-rendered-pr-closed` and has been stale past `STRUCTURALLY_STUCK_TTL_MS` (`plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js`'s `classifyRunDir`). This classification is deliberately visibility-only — `trackStuckSkip` never changes what `archiveMerged` does with the directory (still just skip); it exists solely to escalate a single shared GitHub issue (this one, per `escalate-residue.js`'s #1811 Deliverable 4 — one issue for the whole reason, not one per path) so a human notices directories reconcile has decided it cannot safely resolve on its own.

This record was auto-filed naming exactly one stuck path (`.claude-tweaks/pipelines/2026-09-13T202040-record-1798`), which has since been cleaned up independently — that specific instance is stale and no longer needs action. However, a fresh `bin/hooks.js reconcile --json` run (during this shaping pass) shows the underlying condition is still live: 16 run directories currently classify under a structurally-stuck-eligible reason, several dating back to late August (`2026-08-26T191436-record-573`, `2026-08-27T*` — four more `console-never-rendered-pr-closed` entries, `2026-08-12T204800-tidy-standalone`) — weeks past any reasonable TTL. The escalation mechanism is working as designed; nobody has acted on the directories it's pointing at.

## Deliverables

- Re-enumerate the current candidate set fresh (`bin/hooks.js reconcile --json`'s `runs[]` array, filtered to `action: "skipped"` with `reason` in `no-worktree`/`no-branch`/`no-pr`/`console-never-rendered-pr-closed`) — the list in this record's Current State will have moved again by build time.
- For each candidate, confirm it's genuinely inert before touching it: no live worktree (`git worktree list`), no live local/remote branch matching its run, and — for a PR-linked run — the PR's actual state via `gh pr view` (a `console-never-rendered-pr-closed` classification specifically requires re-confirming the PR is CLOSED, never MERGED, per `archive-merged.js`'s own carve-out comment).
- Archive each confirmed-inert directory via the existing `bin/hooks.js archive-run --run <dir>` mechanism. For any directory that turns out to still hold recoverable unfinished work (a false positive in the staleness classification — e.g. a worktree that exists but reconcile's snapshot didn't see it), leave it and document why in this record's own thread rather than archiving it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every run directory `bin/hooks.js reconcile --json` currently classifies as `structurally-stuck`-eligible (the four reasons above) and past its TTL is either archived or left with a documented reason (posted as a comment on this issue) for why it was deliberately kept.
- A `bin/hooks.js reconcile --json` run after cleanup shows the candidate set has shrunk to zero, or only to directories newly gone stale since this pass began (with a one-line note on why those are out of scope for this pass).
- No `git worktree`/branch that is genuinely still in use gets archived — the live-check above must run before every archival, not be skipped as "probably fine."

## Release Note

Cleaned up run directories that reconcile could never finish because their worktree, branch, or PR was gone.

## Technical Approach

Drive this from `bin/hooks.js reconcile --json`'s own output rather than re-deriving the classification logic by hand — that command already implements `classifyRunDir`'s precedence and TTL rules correctly; this record's job is to act on what it reports, not reimplement it. `bin/hooks.js archive-run --run <dir>` is the existing, tested archival path (used elsewhere in this repo's own housekeeping passes) — reuse it rather than a manual `git mv`.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js` — `classifyRunDir`, `STRUCTURALLY_STUCK_REASONS`, `trackStuckSkip` (read for context, not expected to change unless the investigation above turns up a real classification bug)
- `plugin/bin/hooks.js` — `reconcile --json` and `archive-run --run <dir>` subcommands, the two CLIs this record's work runs against

## Gotchas

- The one path named in this record's auto-filed `<!-- stuck-paths -->` marker has already been cleaned up independently — don't treat it as the thing to fix; re-derive the current list fresh at build time, since it will have shifted again.
- If the investigation above finds a *pattern* rather than isolated stale directories (e.g. every `console-never-rendered-pr-closed` case is provably safe to archive, suggesting reconcile itself should auto-archive that specific reason past its TTL instead of only escalating), that's a legitimate scope expansion worth raising — but the baseline deliverable is the manual cleanup pass above, not a reconcile code change, unless the investigation clearly justifies one.

## Original request

reconcile: structurally-stuck run directories

Reconcile has one or more run directories stuck at `structurally-stuck` (no-worktree/no-branch/no-pr) past the escalation threshold.

<!-- stuck-paths -->
- `/Users/thomasholknielsen/Code Workspaces/claude-tweaks/.claude-tweaks/pipelines/2026-09-13T202040-record-1798`
<!-- /stuck-paths -->

Filed automatically by `bin/lib/reconcile` — see #644/#1811.

Surface: infra

Origin: by:feedback (self-referential session evaluation, /claude-tweaks:feedback bare invocation)

**Related:** #2728

## Current State

Executing `/claude-tweaks:backlog refine` end to end (both its `#N`-filtered and whole-queue forms) in a single session on 2026-09-20 required reading several large `_shared`/skill reference files in full — `refine-lanes.md` (457 lines, confirmed: Resolve, Re-authorize, Grant, Flag-back, Needs-decision, Priority, Dependency-repair, and Needs-you lane templates), `_shared/worktree-setup.md` (296 lines, confirmed: Pre-creation reconcile, Post-creation catch-up, Pre-flight divergence check, and several Windows-specific and headless-ride-along subsections), and `_shared/pipeline-run-dir.md` (288 lines, confirmed: the full Anchoring section including the CLI-argument-boundary guard family, most of which applies to callers other than a standalone `/backlog refine` run). In the narrower `#N`-filtered invocation, only the Priority lane's own rendering rules and the plain worktree fetch+merge ever executed — the Resolve/Grant/Flag-back/Needs-decision templates, the Windows long-path recovery procedure, and the CLI-argument-boundary guard descriptions were all read but never exercised.

## Deliverables

- Where a lazy-loaded sub-file already documents multiple mutually-exclusive branches (as `refine-lanes.md` does per-lane), consider whether a citing skill step can name which branch(es) apply to the resolved invocation shape *before* the read, so a reader can skip straight to the relevant section rather than reading start-to-finish.
- For `_shared/worktree-setup.md` and `_shared/pipeline-run-dir.md` specifically, evaluate whether the Windows-specific recovery procedures and the CLI-argument-boundary guard family (relevant mainly to `bin/*.js` authors, not to a skill-following session) could split into their own sub-files, following the same lazy-load discipline already applied elsewhere in this plugin.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A `/claude-tweaks:backlog refine #N` invocation touching only the Priority lane no longer requires reading Resolve/Grant/Flag-back/Needs-decision lane templates in full to reach the one section it needs.
- Total bytes read from `_shared/worktree-setup.md` and `_shared/pipeline-run-dir.md` during an ordinary worktree-creation catch-up drop measurably versus today's full-file reads, without losing any content a citing skill still needs.

## Release Note

Reduced how much reference material backlog refine loads when only part of it applies.

## Technical Approach

Both deliverables are evaluation tasks first, not a locked-in split — this record's own Acceptance Criteria are measurable outcomes (reduced reads for the common case), not a specific file-split mechanism, so the actual resolution should be judged against those outcomes rather than assumed up front. For `refine-lanes.md`: the citing step in `refine-mode.md` already knows, per invocation shape (`#N`-filtered vs. whole-queue), which lanes it will actually reach — the fix is likely a scoping note at the citation point ("this invocation only reaches the Priority lane section below") rather than restructuring the lane file itself, since the lanes genuinely are mutually exclusive per-record but the file as a whole still needs all of them documented somewhere. For `_shared/worktree-setup.md`/`_shared/pipeline-run-dir.md`: this is the kind of cross-referenced `_shared` file split the `shared-contract-extraction` skill exists to guide — read it before extracting anything, since a shared contract file has multiple citers whose own cross-references must keep resolving after any split.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/backlog/refine-lanes.md` — the 457-line lane-template file; candidate for a citation-site scoping note rather than a structural split
- `plugin/skills/backlog/refine-mode.md` — the citing step that already knows which lane(s) a given invocation shape reaches
- `plugin/skills/_shared/worktree-setup.md` — candidate for splitting out the Windows-specific recovery procedure into its own lazily-loaded sub-file
- `plugin/skills/_shared/pipeline-run-dir.md` — candidate for splitting out the CLI-argument-boundary guard family (relevant to `bin/*.js` authors, not most skill-following sessions) into its own sub-file

## Gotchas

**Related:** #2729

## Current State

`refine-mode.md`'s Step 5 documents the Dependency-repair lane's detection method precisely: attach native blocked-by links via `buildNativeDependencyQuery`, then run `findUnresolvedDependencyProse` over the result (confirmed present in `refine-mode.md`). In a session on 2026-09-20, this mechanized method was not run; instead, every candidate record's body was read directly by hand as part of the priority-lane synthesis pass, and no "blocked by" prose was found in that manual read. The rendered closing summary reported "0 dependency-repair" exactly as it would if the documented mechanized check had run and found nothing — with no line disclosing that a different, less rigorous method actually produced that zero.

## Deliverables

- When a refine run's closing summary reports a lane count for a check whose documented mechanism was not run in full (a manual substitute was used instead), state that substitution inline next to the count — e.g. "0 dependency-repair (manual body read, not the native-link+prose-scan pipeline)" — rather than rendering the same bare count a fully-mechanized run would produce.
- Consider whether this same disclosure obligation applies to any other lane in `refine-mode.md`/`refine-lanes.md` whose detection has more than one implementation path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A refine closing summary distinguishes, per lane, between "checked via the documented mechanism, found nothing" and "checked via a substitute method, found nothing" wherever the two can diverge in confidence.

## Release Note

Made backlog refine's summary say when a check ran by a substitute method instead of the documented one.

## Technical Approach

Extend `refine-closing-summary.md`'s closing-summary render (the same file #2729 targets for its mechanical-tally fix — related, but a distinct concern: that record makes the *count* itself trustworthy, this one makes the *method* behind a zero-or-low count disclosed) to carry an optional method-substitution annotation per lane. The natural point to detect the substitution is wherever `refine-mode.md`'s Step 5 actually invokes (or skips) `buildNativeDependencyQuery`/`findUnresolvedDependencyProse` — if that step's own procedure was bypassed in favor of a manual read, the closing-summary composer needs that fact as an explicit signal (a flag or note carried alongside the lane's own count) rather than inferring it after the fact from `decisions.md`. For the second (exploratory) deliverable, audit every lane in `refine-mode.md`/`refine-lanes.md` for lanes with more than one detection path (mechanized vs. manual/fallback) and decide per-lane whether the same annotation is warranted.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/backlog/refine-closing-summary.md` — the closing-summary render this record adds the method-substitution annotation to
- `plugin/skills/backlog/refine-mode.md` — Step 5's Dependency-repair lane, where the native-link+prose-scan pipeline is documented and where a substitution would need to be flagged
- `plugin/skills/backlog/refine-lanes.md` — candidate location for the cross-lane audit the second deliverable asks for

## Gotchas

- The second deliverable is exploratory ("consider whether...") — the Acceptance Criteria above cover only the Dependency-repair lane explicitly; a build should treat generalizing to other lanes as a judgment call to make and document, not a mandatory expansion.
- This is a disclosure fix, not a correctness fix to the detection itself — a manual read that happens to be accurate still produces a correct "0," this record only asks that the audit trail say which method produced it.

**Related:** #2718, #2719

## Current State

`/claude-tweaks:backlog refine`'s grant sub-stage (`refine-mode.md` Step 3) documents `assess-agent-autonomy grant-check` as a sequential, once-per-record `Skill()` invocation. `grant-check.md`'s own Step 1 caches the fetched record body at a session-tmp path (`assess-grant-{n}.json`, confirmed present) specifically so Step 3.5's body-shape re-verification can reuse it instead of a second `gh issue view` round-trip. On a large batch (this session's whole-queue sweep had 40 grant-check-eligible records), running 40 sequential `Skill()` calls in the main thread is impractical, so the session instead parallelized the pass across 5 ad-hoc Task-agent dispatches — each agent ran its own `gh issue view` calls directly rather than through the documented session-tmp caching path (subagents don't share the orchestrating session's `$CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`-keyed cache directory). Step 3.5 then had to re-fetch every one of the ~34 grant-recommended bodies a second time, exactly the round-trip the cache exists to avoid.

## Deliverables

- Document a sanctioned parallel-fan-out shape for the grant-check pass on a large batch — either a Task-agent dispatch template (mirroring `_shared/subagent-output-contract.md`'s Template A/B/C pattern) that writes each result to a shared, orchestrator-readable location Step 3.5 can still consume, or an explicit statement that grant-check is sequential-only and a caller facing a large batch should reduce via `--budget` rather than parallelize by hand.
- If a fan-out shape is added, specify how Step 3.5's body-cache reuse extends to it (e.g., the dispatch prompt writes the fetched body to the orchestrator's own session-tmp path before returning, rather than only to the subagent's ephemeral context).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A grant-check pass run against a 40-record batch, however dispatched, produces no more than one `gh issue view`/body-fetch round trip per record across the whole grant-check + Step 3.5 pipeline.
- The chosen shape (fan-out template or sequential-only statement) is stated in `refine-mode.md`'s Step 3, not left to be improvised per-caller.

## Release Note

Added a parallel way to run autonomy grant checks on large batches without losing cached record bodies.

## Technical Approach

Decide first whether a fan-out template is actually worth adding, or whether the simpler fix — stating in `refine-mode.md`'s Step 3 that `grant-check` is sequential-only, and that a batch above some size should be split via `--budget` across multiple refine invocations rather than parallelized by hand — is the better tradeoff (mirrors the existing `_shared/subagent-output-contract.md` guidance that dispatch templates cost real overhead and aren't a default). If a fan-out template is chosen instead: the dispatch prompt for each Task-agent must write its fetched record body to the *orchestrator's* session-tmp path (`assess-grant-{n}.json`, the same path `grant-check.md`'s Step 1 already writes to sequentially) before returning its verdict, rather than only holding it in the subagent's own ephemeral context — this is what lets Step 3.5 find and reuse the cached body regardless of which path populated it. Either way, `refine-mode.md`'s Step 3 needs to state the decision explicitly so it isn't re-improvised by the next large-batch session.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/backlog/refine-mode.md` — Step 3, where the grant-check invocation shape (sequential vs. a documented fan-out) needs to be stated
- `plugin/skills/assess-agent-autonomy/grant-check.md` — Step 1's session-tmp caching path (`assess-grant-{n}.json`), which a fan-out shape would need to extend rather than bypass
- `plugin/skills/_shared/subagent-output-contract.md` — the Template A/B/C pattern a fan-out shape would follow, if that's the chosen resolution

## Gotchas

- Don't build a fan-out template speculatively if the simpler "sequential-only, split via `--budget`" resolution is judged sufficient — the Deliverables explicitly offer both, and the Acceptance Criteria are satisfied by either.
- If a fan-out template is added, verify it doesn't reintroduce the exact caching gap this record describes for a *different* consumer — any future step that expects `assess-grant-{n}.json` to exist after a grant-check pass needs the fan-out path to actually write it, not just the sequential path.

## Original request

Surface: infra

Origin: by:feedback (self-referential session evaluation, /claude-tweaks:feedback bare invocation)

**Related:** #2719, #2720

## Current State

`/claude-tweaks:backlog refine`'s grant sub-stage (`refine-mode.md` Step 3) computes its worklist once, then spends real wall-clock time generating a `RECOMMEND_BUILD`/`RECOMMEND_MERGE` judgment (via `assess-agent-autonomy grant-check`) for every candidate in `.grantSlice.selected`, before Step 5's pre-write reverify ever checks whether that judgment's premise still holds. In a session on 2026-09-20, a full whole-queue `/claude-tweaks:backlog refine` sweep computed grant-check judgments for 40 ready-but-ungranted records (parallelized across 5 Task-agent dispatches to make the volume tractable) — and by the time Step 5's reverify ran, a concurrent actor (another session or a scheduled Routine) had already fully processed the entire same 40-record population: every record already carried a `priority:*` label and either a grant (`auto:build`/`auto:merge`) or `needs:decision`. All 40 of this run's freshly computed grant-check judgments were discarded as stale at write time — the reverify step correctly caught the race, but only after the (expensive) judgment pass had already run to completion with no cheaper earlier signal available.

Step 3 already has one comparable pattern at its own entry point: the "Merge-lane circuit breaker reset offer," which reads a best-effort breaker signal before the grant-sweep runs. This record's freshness check is the analogous idea applied to the population itself rather than a breaker flag.

## Deliverables

- Add a cheap, mechanical pre-dispatch freshness check immediately before the grant-check judgment pass fires (e.g., a lightweight `gh issue list --label ready --state open` count/diff against Step 1's own fetched population, or a re-check of just the candidate numbers' current grant/priority state) — when the population has shrunk or already resolved since Step 1's fetch, short-circuit before spending the judgment budget on now-stale candidates, not just before the write.
- Document this check in `refine-mode.md`'s Step 3, alongside the existing merge-lane circuit-breaker offer that already runs at this sub-stage's start.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A grant sub-stage run where the candidate population has already been fully processed by a concurrent actor since Step 1's fetch detects this before dispatching any grant-check judgment calls, and reports the skip plainly instead of running the full judgment pass first.
- A grant sub-stage run where the population is still current (the common case) pays no additional round-trip cost from this check — the freshness probe is cheap relative to the judgment pass it guards.

## Release Note

Added a quick freshness check before backlog refine spends effort on grant checks.

## Technical Approach

Insert the freshness check at the start of `refine-mode.md`'s Step 3, right after the existing merge-lane circuit breaker reset offer and before `.grantSlice.selected` is handed to the per-record `grant-check` dispatch loop. The cheapest option: re-fetch just the label state of the candidate numbers already in `.grantSlice.selected` (a single `gh issue list --state open --json number,labels -q '...'` filtered to those numbers, or an equivalent batched read) and compare against Step 1's own fetched snapshot — if every (or substantially all) candidates already carry a grant or `priority:*`+resolution since that snapshot, short-circuit the whole sub-stage with a plain report line, the same way the circuit-breaker offer already short-circuits on a tripped breaker. This reuses Step 5's own reverify comparison logic conceptually (same "live label state vs. captured premise" check), just run once up front over the whole slice instead of once per record after the judgment pass.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/backlog/refine-mode.md` — Step 3's opening (the merge-lane circuit breaker offer is the closest existing precedent), and the `.grantSlice.selected`/`.grantSlice.remaining` read this check gates
- `plugin/skills/backlog/merge-lane-reset.md` — the existing best-effort breaker-read pattern this check's own "cheap, best-effort, run before the expensive pass" shape mirrors

## Gotchas

- This check is deliberately best-effort and approximate — a population that's *partially* stale (some records resolved, most not) should still proceed with the judgment pass for the records that are still fresh, not abort the whole slice; only a fully- or substantially-resolved population justifies the short-circuit, mirroring the "cheap enough to not matter in the common case" acceptance criterion.
- Don't duplicate Step 5's own pre-write reverify logic wholesale — this is a coarser, cheaper up-front signal to avoid wasted judgment-pass cost, not a replacement for Step 5's own per-record correctness check, which still must run regardless of whether this new check fires.

Surface: infra

# Reflect — staged finding 1

**Category:** tangential

## Origin

refs #2563 (reflect full-mode, Friction lens, this run)

## Current State

`bin/lib/hooks/subagent-stop.js` logs a `contract-violation` event whenever a dispatched agent's reply does not end with the canonical `STATUS: {WORD}` line as its last non-empty line. This run observed 5 such events, every one logged against this dispatched agent's own **interim progress-update replies** sent between async `Agent`-tool notifications while 8 nested review-lens agents (and later, one code-simplifier agent) were completing — e.g. "2 of 8 back. Lens 3b-b (Security) surfaced two HIGH findings...". None of these replies claimed to be a final reply; each one explicitly stated more work was pending, and the dispatch's actual final reply (this run's own eventual STATUS line) does conform. `skills/reflect/full-mode.md`'s own Friction-lens text already anticipates the hook can over-report and names one carve-out ("a dispatch declaring its own first-line contract") — that carve-out doesn't cover this shape: a dispatched agent that must itself fan out to nested async work and yield control across multiple turns before its own final reply, per the `Agent` tool's documented async-notification mechanism (`_shared/subagent-output-contract.md`'s dispatch-facing sections). Every such interim turn currently reads as a false-positive contract violation, and the false-positive count scales with how many nested async agents a dispatch fans out to (5 events from 9 nested dispatches on this run alone).

The detector already has one related filter: `isAsyncWaitSignal`/`asyncWaitCheckpoint` in `subagent-stop.js` suppresses logging when the *immediately preceding* transcript entry is itself an async signal (a task-notification, or a tool result flagged `isAsync: true`) — reply text reacting directly to "a background dispatch just launched or reported in" (#2041). The gap this record describes is narrower: an interim reply composed after the agent has already done other work following that signal (dispatching further nested agents, reading their output) no longer has an async signal as its immediately preceding entry, so the existing filter doesn't catch it even though the reply is still legitimately mid-dispatch, not a final answer.

## Deliverables

2. `skills/reflect/full-mode.md`'s Friction-lens carve-out list is updated to name this case explicitly (or superseded once the detector itself handles it), so a future reflect pass does not need to re-derive the same "these were never real violations" judgment call from scratch.

Surface: infra

## Current State

The pr-first integration path's auto-merge convention (`_shared/pr-first-merge.md`, or the calling skill that invokes it) calls `gh pr merge {n} --auto --squash` when a PR's status checks are still `IN_PROGRESS`, then reports the outcome as "merged once CI passed" based solely on the PR's `state` transitioning to `MERGED`. `gh pr merge --auto` merges immediately once GitHub's own merge-readiness conditions are satisfied — which, on a repository with no *required* status checks configured, can mean immediately, regardless of whether an in-progress check later passes or fails. The reporting language ("queue an auto-merge so it merges once that passes") implies the merge is gated on that specific check's conclusion, but nothing in the sequence ever reads that check's final `conclusion` field to confirm it actually passed before or as part of the merge. Concretely observed: `test` check `IN_PROGRESS` at 18:50:21Z, "I'll queue an auto-merge so it merges once that passes" at 18:50:28Z, `gh pr merge --auto --squash` at 18:50:31Z, PR `state: MERGED` at `mergedAt: 2026-09-20T18:50:30Z` — merged 9 seconds after the check was last observed in progress, with no subsequent read of that check's conclusion.

## Deliverables

- In `_shared/pr-first-merge.md` (or wherever the `--auto` merge call and its result reporting are documented), require reading the relevant status check's `conclusion` (via `gh pr view --json statusCheckRollup`) after a `gh pr merge --auto` call resolves to `MERGED`, and state explicitly in the reported outcome whether the check had actually completed and passed by then, or whether the repository has no required checks and the merge proceeded independent of the check's state.
- Note in that file that `gh pr merge --auto` on a repo with no required checks is not equivalent to "wait for checks to pass" — name this distinction explicitly so a caller doesn't infer gating behavior that isn't there.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A caller following `_shared/pr-first-merge.md`'s auto-merge procedure reads and reports the actual check conclusion (or its absence/irrelevance) rather than inferring "merged once CI passed" from the PR's `state` field alone.
- The file states plainly whether this repository's branch protection requires the `test` check before merge, so future callers don't have to re-derive that fact per-run.

## Release Note

Made auto-merge reporting read the actual check result before calling a merge green.

## Technical Approach

Locate the `--auto`-merge call site in `_shared/pr-first-merge.md` and add a post-merge (or, where the merge is not yet resolved, a post-arm) read of `gh pr view {n} --json statusCheckRollup` to extract the named check's `conclusion`. Compose the reported outcome from that read rather than from the PR's `state` alone: "merged, {check} concluded {conclusion}" when a required check resolved before merge, or "merged — this repository has no required status checks, so the merge did not wait on {check}'s outcome" when it doesn't. Add a one-time note near the top of the auto-merge procedure documenting this repository's actual branch-protection configuration (required checks or their absence) so this doesn't need re-deriving per run.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/_shared/pr-first-merge.md` — the `--auto` merge call and its result-reporting language

## Gotchas

- This is a reporting-fidelity fix, not a merge-mechanics change — do not add an actual wait-for-check-conclusion gate unless the record's own scope is later widened; the Acceptance Criteria only ask for accurate reporting of what already happened.
- Verify the actual branch-protection state (`gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches/{branch}/protection` or the repo settings UI) rather than assuming from this record's evidence alone — the observed 9-second merge is consistent with "no required checks" but should be confirmed directly before documenting it as fact.

Surface: terminal

## Current State

Across at least three call sites, a stop asks the user to confirm something a prior input or a resolved project policy had already decided, rather than proceeding or presenting it as a read-only FYI:

1. **A pasted Next Actions-style list with an explicit `(recommended)` marker on one line** is not treated as an implicit selection — the consuming skill still asks "which of these should I run?" with that same line pre-marked Recommended, even though the marker's whole purpose (per `docs/skill-authoring.md`'s Skill handoffs convention — recommended-first, paste-ready commands) is to let a human paste the line they want without further ceremony.
2. **`superpowers:brainstorming`'s scope-assessment step**, when a design's framing could go two ways (e.g. "should we also weigh approach X"), asks a stop specifically to gate *whether to consider* an approach, immediately followed by a second stop asking *which approach to choose* — the first is subsumed by the second and could be folded into one question with the alternative as one of the offered options.
3. **`_shared/pr-first-merge.md`'s (or the calling skill's) merge-path question** ("push + open a PR" vs "merge locally") is asked even when `.claude-tweaks/policy.yml`'s `integration-model: pr-first` has already resolved which applies — CLAUDE.md states this resolution should never be re-derived ad hoc ("Never re-derive which one applies ad hoc — read the resolution, once, per that file"), which by extension means it should not be re-asked as an open choice either once resolved.

Measured on one session: 8 `AskUserQuestion` stops (9 questions) across 5 substantive user turns; 9 of 9 resolved to the pre-marked Recommended option; of the 8 stops, 3 fell into the pattern above.

## Deliverables

- Wherever a skill renders a `## Next Actions`-style block with a `(recommended)`/`(Recommended)` marker and later re-consumes that same text as raw input (e.g. via a paste), treat the marked line as the default selection when the paste is unambiguous, rather than re-asking which option to run.
- In `superpowers:brainstorming`'s scope-assessment guidance (or the calling skill's own framing step, if this repo layers one on top), fold a "should we also weigh approach X" gate into the immediately-following "which approach" question, offering X as one of the presented options instead of gating access to it with a separate prior stop.
- In whichever skill/shared file renders the merge-path question after `_shared/pr-first-merge.md`'s (or `_shared/integration-model.md`'s) resolution is already known, replace the question with a one-line FYI ("Integration model: pr-first — pushing and opening a PR") and proceed, reserving an actual question for the case where no policy value resolves.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A paste containing a single `(recommended)`/`(Recommended)`-marked line is not re-confirmed via a fresh `AskUserQuestion` when the paste is otherwise unambiguous (no competing marked line, no additional free text implying a different choice).
- Brainstorming's scope-assessment and approach-choice questions collapse into one `AskUserQuestion` call when they would otherwise be sequential and the first is fully subsumed by the second.
- A merge-path decision governed by a resolved `integration-model` policy value renders as a read-only FYI line, not an `AskUserQuestion`, in the default case.

## Release Note

Stopped skills from re-asking decisions that earlier input or project policy already answered.

## Technical Approach

Three independent, separately-verifiable fixes sharing one root cause (a stop re-asks a decision that upstream input or policy already made):

1. **Next Actions paste recognition** — wherever a skill's entry point parses free-text input that could be a pasted Next Actions block (the shape `docs/skill-authoring.md`'s Skill handoffs convention defines), detect a single `(recommended)`/`(Recommended)`-marked line with no competing marker and treat it as the selection, skipping the re-confirmation `AskUserQuestion` for that ambiguity-free case only.
2. **Brainstorming scope-assessment merge** — locate the two sequential stops (a "should we consider X" gate immediately followed by "which approach") in `superpowers:brainstorming`'s scope-assessment guidance, and merge them into one `AskUserQuestion` call whose options include X directly, removing the prior gating question.
3. **Merge-path FYI** — locate the merge-path `AskUserQuestion` in `_shared/pr-first-merge.md` (or its caller) and gate it on whether `integration-model` already resolved to a definite value (`_shared/integration-model.md`'s resolution); when it has, render a one-line FYI and proceed instead of asking.

Each fix should be independently testable against a captured session transcript exhibiting the pattern (the Original request cites concrete evidence for all three), and none should suppress the underlying question when the resolving input is genuinely ambiguous or absent.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/_shared/pr-first-merge.md` — the merge-path question, gated on `integration-model` resolution
- `plugin/skills/superpowers:brainstorming` (or this repo's own framing layer on top of it, if any) — the scope-assessment / approach-choice stop merge
- `plugin/docs/skill-authoring.md` — the `(recommended)` marker convention this fix relies on for paste recognition

## Gotchas

- Fix 1 (Next Actions paste recognition) must stay narrow: only collapse the question when the paste is genuinely unambiguous (one marked line, no competing signal in the free text) — a paste with additional context implying a different choice should still ask.
- Fix 2 (brainstorming merge) touches `superpowers:brainstorming`, an upstream dependency this plugin does not own — verify whether the scope-assessment step lives in superpowers itself or in a claude-tweaks layer on top before deciding where the fix lands; an upstream-only fix may need to be filed against that plugin instead of implemented here.
- Fix 3 (merge-path FYI) must still ask when `integration-model` resolves to nothing (an unresolved/ambiguous case) — the FYI-only path applies exclusively when CLAUDE.md's own resolution note says the value is already known.

Surface: infra

## Current State

`wrap-up-engine.js render --section console` fails with no diagnostic output when the run's `record` step was never invoked after `plan` — a caller who performs per-row judgment out-of-band (e.g. via separate `stage-item.js`/`log-decision.js` calls instead of feeding a structured payload back into the engine) gets no indication of what precondition is missing. Observed twice in one session: `--strict` exits 2 with completely empty stdout/stderr; without `--strict` it exits 0 with empty output. Either way there is no actionable signal, and the caller has to infer from source reading that a `record` call was expected and never made — cost roughly 10 extra tool calls reading procedure files and hand-composing the Review Console content instead of one working render call.

## Deliverables

- `render --section console` detects a missing/empty engine-state (no prior `record` call for this run-dir) and fails loud with a specific, actionable message — e.g. "no engine-state.json found for this run-dir — run `record` first."
- This applies under both `--strict` and non-strict invocation: neither mode should produce silent empty output.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Running `render --section console --strict` against a run-dir with a `plan` output but no `record` call exits non-zero with a non-empty, actionable error message naming the missing precondition.
- Running the same command without `--strict` also produces the actionable message (not silent exit 0 with empty output).
- Running `render --section console` against a run-dir that DID complete `record` is unaffected — this fix only changes the missing-precondition path.

## Release Note

Made the wrap-up engine fail with a clear message when its console is rendered before any results were recorded.

## Technical Approach

Locate `render`'s entry point in `plugin/bin/wrap-up-engine.js` (the `--section console` handler) and its read of the run-dir's engine-state file. Add a precondition check before rendering: if the expected engine-state artifact (written by the `record` step) is absent or empty, exit with a clear error naming the missing precondition and the remedy (`run record first`), on both `--strict` and non-strict paths — today the two paths differ only in exit code, both leaving stdout/stderr empty, so the fix should apply the same message to both rather than only fixing one.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/wrap-up-engine.js` — `render --section console` handler and its engine-state read

## Gotchas

- Don't conflate "missing engine-state" with "engine-state present but empty" — both need actionable messages, but a caller reading the error should be able to tell whether `record` was never run at all versus ran but produced nothing.
- Keep the fix scoped to detecting and reporting the missing precondition — do not add a fallback that silently synthesizes a Review Console from a `plan`-only run-dir, which would mask the same problem this fix exists to surface.

## Original request

bin/wrap-up-engine.js: render fails silently when the plan/record sequence was skipped

**Summary:** `wrap-up-engine.js render --section console` fails with no diagnostic output at all when the run's `record` step was never invoked after `plan` — a caller who performs the per-row judgment out-of-band (e.g. via separate `stage-item.js`/`log-decision.js` calls instead of feeding a structured payload back into the engine) gets no indication of what precondition is missing.

**Kind:** Defect

**Affected component:** `bin/wrap-up-engine.js` (`render --section console`)

**Objective:** Friction

**Measurement:** 2 failed render attempts this session (one `--strict` exit 2 with no output, one non-strict exit 0 with empty output) before abandoning the deterministic path for a hand-composed one.

**Cost this session:** roughly 10 extra tool calls reading procedure files and improvising the Review Console's content by hand instead of one working render call.

**Repro steps:**
1. Run `wrap-up-engine.js plan --run-dir <dir> --base <sha> --ceremony standard` — produces a registry plan JSON with several rows (Skills, Docs, Journeys, CLAUDE.md & rules, Decision records, Broken references, Memory, Upstream feedback).
2. Skip the `record` step entirely — perform the judgment for each open-gated row directly (e.g. staging a finding via `stage-item.js` and logging the decision via `log-decision.js`) rather than composing a structured payload and piping it into `wrap-up-engine.js record --run-dir <dir>`.
3. Run `wrap-up-engine.js render --run-dir <dir> --section console --strict`.

**Expected vs. actual:**
Expected: a clear, actionable error naming the missing precondition — e.g. "no engine-state.json found for this run-dir — run `record` first."
Actual: with `--strict`, the command exits 2 with completely empty stdout/stderr. Without `--strict`, it exits 0 with empty output. Either way, there is no information about what is wrong or what to do about it — the caller has to infer from source reading that a `record` call was expected and never made.

**Proposed fix:** `render` should detect a missing/empty engine-state (no prior `record` call) and fail loud with a specific, actionable message, rather than a bare non-zero exit or silent empty output.

**Definition:** Clear.

groups.body:
Surface: infra

## Current State
`plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/engine-verify.js`'s `carrier-commit` check (`registerCheck('carrier-commit', …)`, line ~320) verifies that each resolved issue in a wrap-up run has a "carrier commit" that closed it. The check currently greps the branch log for the literal string `Fixes #{n}` only (line ~330: `deps.git(['log', '--grep=Fixes #${n}', ...])`), and, when a PR-first fallback is needed, checks the PR body for the same literal string (line ~345: `prBody.includes('Fixes #${n}')`).

GitHub recognizes a broader set of closing keywords in commit messages and PR bodies — `close`, `closes`, `closed`, `fix`, `fixes`, `fixed`, `resolve`, `resolves`, `resolved` (case-insensitive, optionally `owner/repo#N`) — any of which actually closes the linked issue on merge. Because this check only recognizes the literal `Fixes #N` form, a run whose commits used any other recognized keyword (e.g. `Closes #N`) fails the check with `missing` populated for every record, even though GitHub's own state shows the issues correctly closed. This was observed on a real four-record standalone wrap-up (commits used `Closes #N`; all four issues were CLOSED at merge time; `verify` still exited 3 and `execution-and-verification.md`'s exit-3 → BLOCKED rule fired incorrectly), on plugin 6.127.0.

The repo already has a reusable mechanism for checking an issue's actual closing state via GraphQL: `plugin/bin/lib/issues/linked-prs.js`'s `fetchLinkedPRs` resolves each candidate issue's `closedByPullRequestsReferences` connection in one batched call — this is the "ground truth" data source the bug report's proposed fix references.

A related, separately-tracked false-negative in the same verify table is #2552 (`run-dir-archived`) — not in scope here, but worth being aware the verify table has more than one known false-negative row.

## Deliverables
1. Replace the `carrier-commit` check's branch-log grep (line ~330) with a case-insensitive match over GitHub's full recognized closing-keyword set (`close`, `closes`, `closed`, `fix`, `fixes`, `fixed`, `resolve`, `resolves`, `resolved`), each optionally preceded by `owner/repo` before the `#N`, matching against `#{n}` as a whole reference (not a substring of a larger number).
2. Apply the same keyword-set widening to the PR-body fallback check (line ~345), which currently has the identical literal-`Fixes` narrowing.
3. Add a ground-truth fallback: when neither the branch-log grep nor the PR-body check finds a carrier commit for an issue, query the issue's actual state via `gh issue view N --json state` (or reuse `plugin/bin/lib/issues/linked-prs.js`'s `fetchLinkedPRs`/`closedByPullRequestsReferences` connection) and treat a CLOSED state backed by a closing PR/commit reference as a pass on its own, rather than failing purely because no commit message matched a keyword pattern.
4. Keep the existing `fail` behavior for a genuinely-open issue with no matching commit and no closing reference — the fix narrows false negatives, it does not weaken the check's ability to catch a real missing carrier commit.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `carrier-commit` passes for a run whose closing commit message uses any of GitHub's recognized closing keywords (`close`, `closes`, `closed`, `fix`, `fixes`, `fixed`, `resolve`, `resolves`, `resolved`), case-insensitive, with or without an `owner/repo#N` prefix — not just the literal `Fixes #N` form.
- The PR-body fallback check recognizes the same keyword set as the branch-log check (no longer just `Fixes #N`).
- `carrier-commit` passes for an issue that is CLOSED with a `closedByPullRequestsReferences`/closing-commit reference, even if no commit message in the branch range matched any keyword pattern textually (the ground-truth fallback).
- `carrier-commit` still fails (`missing` populated) for an issue with no matching commit message, no matching PR body reference, and no closing-PR-reference-backed CLOSED state — a genuinely missing carrier commit is still caught.
- `tests/bin-lib/wrap-up/engine-verify.test.js` gains test cases covering: a `Closes #N` commit (currently would fail, should now pass), a `Resolves #N` commit, case-insensitivity (`FIXES #N`), and the ground-truth CLOSED-state fallback path.
- Existing passing test cases in `tests/bin-lib/wrap-up/engine-verify.test.js` for the `carrier-commit` check (including the literal `Fixes #N` case) continue to pass.

## Release Note

Fixed wrap-up missing closing keywords other than Fixes when checking the merge commit.

## Technical Approach
Read `plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/engine-verify.js` lines ~306-345 (the `carrier-commit` check and its preceding comment block) and `tests/bin-lib/wrap-up/engine-verify.test.js`'s existing `carrier-commit` test cases before changing anything, to preserve the check's existing pr-first/local-merge branching logic (the comment block above the check, lines ~312-318, explains why the PR-body fallback exists only when `resolvePrNumber` resolves a PR — don't disturb that branching, only the keyword-matching and add the new ground-truth fallback). Build the keyword regex once (a shared constant, since it's needed in three places: the git log `--grep`, the PR body match, and potentially reused by any other check that does closing-keyword matching) rather than inlining it three times. For the ground-truth fallback, reuse `plugin/bin/lib/issues/linked-prs.js`'s existing `fetchLinkedPRs` rather than writing a new GraphQL query — it already resolves `closedByPullRequestsReferences` in one batched call across all candidate issues, matching this check's existing per-issue loop shape.

### Key Files
- `plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/engine-verify.js` — widen the `--grep` pattern (line ~330) and the PR-body check (line ~345) to the full keyword set; add the ground-truth CLOSED-state fallback to `registerCheck('carrier-commit', ...)`
- `plugin/bin/lib/issues/linked-prs.js` — reuse `fetchLinkedPRs` for the ground-truth fallback rather than writing new GraphQL query logic
- `tests/bin-lib/wrap-up/engine-verify.test.js` — add test cases for the widened keyword set, case-insensitivity, and the ground-truth fallback path; verify no regression on the existing `Fixes #N` case

## Gotchas
- Preserve the existing pr-first/local-merge branching logic (the comment at lines ~312-318) — the fix is about widening keyword matching and adding a ground-truth fallback, not restructuring when the PR-body check applies vs. the branch-log check.
- The keyword regex must match `#N` as a whole issue reference, not a substring of a larger number (e.g. `#12` should not match inside `#123`) — use a word boundary or equivalent anchor.
- `owner/repo#N` is a valid GitHub closing-keyword form too (per the bug report) — the regex/match should account for it, not just bare `#N`.
- The ground-truth fallback adds a `gh` (or GraphQL) call — keep it scoped to only the issues that fail the textual match, not run unconditionally for every issue, to avoid unnecessary API calls on the common case where the textual match already succeeds.
- #2552 (`run-dir-archived`) is a separate, already-filed false-negative in the same verify table — do not fold its fix into this record; it has its own scope.

## Original request

wrap-up verify: carrier-commit check only matches the literal "Fixes #N", missing GitHub's other closing keywords

**Summary:** `wrap-up-engine.js verify`'s `carrier-commit` check greps the branch log for the literal `Fixes #N` only, so a run whose closing commits used GitHub's other closing keywords (`Closes #N`, `Resolves #N`, `Fixed #N`, etc.) fails the check even though GitHub closed the issues on merge.

**Kind:** Defect

**Affected component:** `bin/lib/wrap-up/engine-verify.js` (`registerCheck('carrier-commit', …)`), and the `skills/wrap-up/execution-and-verification.md` exit-3 → BLOCKED rule that consumes it

**Repro steps:**
1. On a `local-merge` project, fix a record in a worktree and commit with a footer line `Closes #N` (GitHub's documented closing keyword) instead of `Fixes #N`.
2. Rebase-merge to the integration branch; GitHub closes issue #N.
3. Run `/claude-tweaks:wrap-up #N`; at Phase 4's Verify step, `node bin/wrap-up-engine.js verify --run-dir <run-dir> --base <sha>`.

**Expected vs. actual:**
Expected: `carrier-commit` passes — the range contains a commit whose message closes #N with any keyword GitHub recognizes (`close`, `closes`, `closed`, `fix`, `fixes`, `fixed`, `resolve`, `resolves`, `resolved`, case-insensitive, optionally `owner/repo#N`), and the issue is in fact closed.
Actual: `deps.git(['log', '--grep=Fixes #N', …])` finds nothing, `missing` fills with every record, the row reads `fail — no carrier commit found for #N, …`, verify exits 3, and the skill's rule forbids the closure line on a run that closed all its records. Observed on a four-record standalone wrap-up (commits used `Closes #N`; all four issues showed CLOSED at merge time), plugin 6.127.0.

Proposed fix: match with a case-insensitive regex over GitHub's closing-keyword set (`--grep` with `-i -E '(close[sd]?|fix(e[sd])?|resolve[sd]?) #N\b'`, or read the log once and match in JS), and — since the issue's own state is the ground truth — treat a `gh issue view N --json state` of CLOSED with a `closedByPullRequestsReferences`/closing-commit reference as a pass on its own. The PR-body fallback has the same literal-`Fixes` narrowing (`prBody.includes('Fixes #N')`) and should use the same set.

**Related:** #2552 (run-dir-archived, the other false-negative row in the same verify table)

**Definition:** Clear

**Plugin version:** 6.127.0

Surface: infra

## Current State

Plugin4Shell is a documented zero-click RCE affecting the top four coding agents, exploited through a malicious skill or MCP integration reaching further (filesystem, network, or credentials) than the host session intended (https://www.air.security/blog-posts/plugin4shell). `/claude-tweaks:assess-agent-autonomy`'s `grant-check` mode (`skills/assess-agent-autonomy/grant-check.md`) already judges whether a record's *content* warrants `auto:build`/`auto:merge`, but nothing in the grant chain inspects what a skill or MCP server *can technically reach* — filesystem paths, outbound network, secrets/env — before that grant is extended to unattended (routine) execution. A broad-reach skill and a narrow-reach skill are graded identically today.

## Deliverables

- A reachability-audit lens: a standalone checklist or mechanized script that inventories what a given skill/plugin manifest or MCP server config can touch — filesystem paths (read/write scope), outbound network (domains/ports it can reach), and secrets/env vars it can read.
- Wiring from `grant-check.md`'s Step 2 (Judge) into this lens: a broad-reach verdict downgrades the autonomy recommendation (e.g. `RECOMMEND_BUILD: false`, or a ceiling-clamped grant) rather than being silently ignored.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The lens runs standalone against a skill/plugin manifest or MCP server config and produces a reachability summary (paths, network, secrets) with no other side effects.
- `grant-check.md`'s Step 1 (Gather) or Step 2 (Judge) consults the lens's output before recommending an unattended/routine grant, and a broad-reach verdict measurably changes the recommendation (not just an informational note).
- The lens has a `node --test` suite covering at minimum: a narrow-reach skill (passes clean), a broad-reach skill (flags filesystem/network/secrets separately), and a malformed/unreadable manifest (fails closed, never silently passes).

## Technical Approach

Add the lens as a new `bin/lib/` module (e.g. `bin/lib/issues/reachability-audit.js` or a sibling directory, following this repo's existing `bin/lib/{concern}/` convention) that statically inspects a skill's frontmatter/tool-allowlist and any MCP server config for filesystem/network/secret-reaching declarations — this is a static manifest read, not a live sandbox probe, consistent with the rest of `assess-agent-autonomy`'s content-only judgment style (no subagent dispatch, no execution of the audited skill). Wire it into `grant-check.md`'s existing Step 1/Step 2 flow as an additional signal alongside the record body/labels already gathered there, following the same could-not-gather / gathered-but-inconclusive error-handling shape `SKILL.md`'s Error Handling section already documents for this skill's other modes (conservative default on any read failure, never resolved toward more autonomy).

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/assess-agent-autonomy/grant-check.md` — wire the new lens into Step 1 (Gather) and Step 2 (Judge)
- `plugin/skills/assess-agent-autonomy/SKILL.md` — Error Handling section's conservative-default table, if the lens introduces a new could-not-gather case
- `plugin/bin/lib/` — new module implementing the reachability-audit lens itself (path TBD at build time, following the existing `bin/lib/{concern}/` convention)

## Gotchas

- The lens is a static-manifest read, not a live capability probe — it can only flag *declared* reach (tool allowlists, MCP server config), not runtime behavior a skill's own code might exhibit beyond what it declares. State this limitation explicitly wherever the lens's output is surfaced, so a clean reachability summary is never read as a guarantee of safety.
- Scope this to claude-tweaks' own skill/MCP surface first (the `assess-agent-autonomy` call site) rather than attempting a general-purpose security-scanning tool — the Acceptance Criteria are about gating this repo's own unattended-authorization chain, not shipping a standalone product.

## Original request

Add a reachability audit lens for skill/MCP routine authorization

Current State:
- Plugin4Shell is a zero-click RCE found in the top four coding agents, exploited through a malicious skill or MCP integration reaching further than intended.
- claude-tweaks authorizes skills/plugins for unattended routine jobs (assess-agent-autonomy, backlog auto:build/auto:merge) without a documented check on what filesystem, network, or credential surface a given skill or MCP server can actually reach.

Deliverables:
- A reachability-audit lens (checklist or skill) that inventories what a skill/MCP integration can touch -- filesystem paths, outbound network, secrets/env -- before it is granted routine (unattended) authorization.
- Wire the lens into assess-agent-autonomy so a broad-reach skill downgrades the autonomy grant.

Acceptance Criteria:
- The lens runs standalone and reports a reachability summary for a given skill/plugin manifest.
- assess-agent-autonomy consults it before recommending an unattended/routine grant.

Source: https://www.air.security/blog-posts/plugin4shell

Surface: infra

**Related:** #2624, #2625, #2751

## Current State

The pre-launch security checklist from #2624 landed (PR #2774). Its two main pieces:

- `plugin/skills/_shared/criteria-security-hardening.md`: a criteria fragment. It has "What the generator hands you", "What to flag", "What NOT to flag", "Scope boundary", and "Severity calibration" sections, plus "Copy-paste prompts (one per check, runnable standalone)" lettered (a)–(c).
- `plugin/bin/lib/code-health/candidates-security-hardening.js`: a static generator that emits `{ file, kind, evidence }` candidates. It has one `scan*` function per kind, driven by directory and signal regexes such as `ROUTE_DIR_RE` and `AI_GUARD_SIGNAL_RE`.

The criteria file is registered in `plugin/bin/lib/code-health/criteria.js` as the `security-hardening` focus, and the generator is loaded by `focus-generators.js`. Tests live in `tests/bin-lib/code-health/candidates-security-hardening.test.js`.

It covers exactly three kinds today: `client-secret`, `missing-ownership-check`, and `unguarded-ai-endpoint`. Three well-known gaps from a transcribed source (Instagram Reel) are uncovered, each with a standard mitigation:

1. **XSS via unescaped output.** User-submitted text rendered into HTML without escaping runs script in another user's session.
2. **Unrestricted file uploads.** An upload handler with no type/size validation, served from an executable path, can lead to remote code execution.
3. **Unverified payment webhooks.** A "payment succeeded" callback (e.g. Stripe) accepted without verifying its signature can be forged.

## Deliverables

1. Three new candidate kinds in `candidates-security-hardening.js`, each with its own `scan*` function and signal regexes, flagging only when no mitigating signal appears nearby:
   - `unescaped-output`: raw-HTML sinks such as `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, `innerHTML =`, `v-html`, `{!! !!}`, or `| safe` with no sanitizer signal.
   - `unrestricted-upload`: upload middleware or handlers such as `multer`, `formidable`, `busboy`, `request.files`, or `UploadFile` with no type or size limit signal.
   - `unverified-webhook`: webhook route files with no signature-verification signal such as `constructEvent`, `verifySignature`, `timingSafeEqual`, or a `*-signature` header check.
2. `criteria-security-hardening.md` extended for the three kinds:
   - "What the generator hands you" lists six kinds.
   - "What to flag", "What NOT to flag", and "Severity calibration" each gain entries for the new kinds.
   - "Copy-paste prompts" gains (d), (e), and (f) in the same voice as (a)–(c).
3. The cross-reference: the file's header line cites #2668 alongside #2624, and "Scope boundary" names the three added checks.
4. Generator tests for each new kind: one vulnerable fixture that is flagged, and one mitigated fixture (sanitized output, validated upload, signature-verified webhook) that is not.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `candidatesSecurityHardening` emits `unescaped-output`, `unrestricted-upload`, and `unverified-webhook` candidates for the vulnerable fixtures, and emits none of the three for the mitigated fixtures.
- The existing three kinds' test cases still pass unchanged.
- `criteria-security-hardening.md` lists all six kinds in "What the generator hands you". Each new kind has a "What to flag" entry, a "What NOT to flag" entry, and a "Severity calibration" entry, plus a runnable copy-paste prompt (d)–(f) that names file, line, and fix like prompts (a)–(c).
- The criteria header cites both #2624 and #2668.
- `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

Added security-hardening checks that flag unescaped HTML output, unrestricted file uploads, and unverified payment webhooks.

## Technical Approach

Follow the existing generator's shape: a per-kind `scan*` function that matches a sink or handler regex on route or client files, then checks a text window (`windowAround`) for a mitigating-signal regex before pushing a candidate. Read `scanUnguardedAiEndpoint` first as the closest model (sink present, guard absent). Then write the criteria entries and prompts by reading prompts (a)–(c) and matching their structure.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/code-health/candidates-security-hardening.js` — three new `scan*` functions and their signal regexes
- `plugin/skills/_shared/criteria-security-hardening.md` — new kinds across every section, prompts (d)–(f), header and scope-boundary cross-reference
- `tests/bin-lib/code-health/candidates-security-hardening.test.js` — vulnerable and mitigated fixtures per new kind
- `plugin/bin/lib/code-health/criteria.js` — reference only; the `security-hardening` entry already routes to the fragment

## Gotchas

- Siblings #2663 (legal/compliance questions) and #2666 (secrets-manager and rotation check) extend the same two files. Build them sequentially, not in parallel groups, or expect merge conflicts in the kind list and the prompt lettering.
- This record is stamped `size:low` / `ceremony:fast-lane` from before shaping, when it read as prose-only. With three generator kinds plus tests it is closer to medium. Confirm at `/claude-tweaks:backlog refine` before granting.
- Keep the checks stack-agnostic. The signal lists should cover several frameworks and read as "a mitigation is visibly present", not require one vendor's API.
- A static scan only sees the absence of a recognized mitigation, the same limitation the existing ownership and AI-endpoint checks document. Say so in the new "What NOT to flag" entries.

## Original request

Add XSS / upload / webhook-signature checks to security checklist

Current State:
- Reel (hook-only caption; transcribed) names three vibecoding security holes with fixes: (1) XSS — user-submitted text (comments, usernames) rendered unescaped lets an attacker run code in other users' browsers; fix: sanitize/escape all user input before render; (2) unrestricted file uploads — no type/size check lets an attacker upload an executable file that takes over the server; fix: validate file type and size, store uploads somewhere they can't be executed; (3) unverified payment webhooks — trusting a "payment succeeded" message without verifying it's really from Stripe lets someone fake a successful payment; fix: verify the webhook signature.
- Directly extends the pre-launch security checklist (#2624), which doesn't currently cover input sanitization, upload handling, or webhook verification.

Deliverables:
- Add the three checks to #2624 with copy-paste prompts, matching the pipeline's existing pattern.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Running the check against a sample app flags a violation in each of the three categories when present.
- Docs cross-reference #2624.

Source: https://www.instagram.com/reel/DbeQK4Lp9jF/



**Trigger:** #2624 merges

Surface: infra

**Related:** #2655, #2692, #2706, #2707, #2709, #2765

## Current State

Two social-media Reels describe the same problem: AI-generated app and website design is instantly recognizable because it converges on the same visual tells.

Reel `DcrqbqZRVvC` (transcribed) lists them:

- purple-to-blue gradients and gradient hero text
- emoji in headings
- glassmorphism cards
- low-contrast dark mode
- three-icon-boxes-in-a-row layouts and badge-above-headline
- Lucide icons everywhere and untouched shadcn components
- scroll-triggered fade-ins, cursor-following elements, and hover-fade buttons
- inconsistent spacing
- em-dashes everywhere and generic buzzwords
- serif-italic accent words and the Space Grotesque + Instrument Serif font pairing
- grain texture overlays

Reel `DcjAVGRBmSC` (Showit) adds "gradient blobs, circle icons, bento grids, fake testimonials".

The blocker on hosting has cleared. #2655 landed (PR #2774) as `plugin/skills/visual-review/ux-heuristics-lens.md`: a criteria-only checklist table (`Heuristic | What it flags | Example violation`) invoked from `plugin/skills/visual-review/page-mode.md`'s Step 4 structured analysis, gated on `Surface: web/mobile/desktop`. It is listed in `plugin/skills/visual-review/SKILL.md`'s Page mode bullet and in `docs/plugin-structure.md`'s visual-review sub-file row. That is the hosting pattern this checklist follows.

No claude-tweaks skill enumerates these tells today. Impeccable's design critique (`impeccable:impeccable`, `impeccable-finish-reviewer`) judges overall quality against a chosen world, not a named list of AI-generated tells.

## Deliverables

1. `plugin/skills/visual-review/ai-design-tells-lens.md`: a criteria-only lens in the same shape as `ux-heuristics-lens.md` (intro, "When this lens applies", the checklist table, "Reporting a finding"). The table has one row per deduplicated tell from both Reels, with columns `Tell | Why it reads as generic | Swap it for`.
2. The lens states the source framing: fix a tell by swapping the generic pattern for something specific to the product (real photos, real numbers, real copy), not by polishing the same pattern. It also marks which rows are code-inspectable (gradients, the font pairing) and which need judgment (spacing, buzzwords), and notes that the list is time-bound and needs periodic refresh.
3. `page-mode.md` Step 4 applies this lens right after the UX heuristics lens, with findings reported as `Source = AI Design Tells` in the Step 6 table, under the same `Surface: web/mobile/desktop` gate.
4. `plugin/skills/visual-review/SKILL.md`'s Page mode bullet and `docs/plugin-structure.md`'s visual-review sub-file row list the new file.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `ai-design-tells-lens.md` has one row for every tell listed in Current State: each item from the first Reel's list, plus gradient blobs, circle icons, bento grids, and fake testimonials from the second, merged where they overlap.
- Every row's "Swap it for" cell names product-specific corrective content, not only "avoid this".
- The lens marks each row as code-inspectable or judgment, and states that it needs periodic refresh.
- `page-mode.md` Step 4 cites `ai-design-tells-lens.md` with the `Source = AI Design Tells` reporting label, gated on `Surface: web/mobile/desktop`.
- `visual-review/SKILL.md` and `docs/plugin-structure.md` both name the new file.
- The PR description records a manual dry run: the lens applied to a sample UI snippet with a purple-to-blue gradient hero and an emoji heading flags both tells by name, and applied to a snippet with none of the tells flags nothing.
- `npm test` passes, including the conformance suites that pin `docs/plugin-structure.md`'s sub-file table and `visual-review` prose.

## Release Note

Added an AI-generated-design-tells checklist to visual review that flags generic patterns such as purple-to-blue gradients and emoji headings, with product-specific alternatives for each.

## Technical Approach

Copy `ux-heuristics-lens.md`'s section structure and gate wording so the two lenses read as siblings. Deduplicate the second Reel's narrative items into the first Reel's list (gradient blobs extend the gradient row; circle icons extend the icon row; bento grids and fake testimonials become their own rows). Wire the lens into `page-mode.md` Step 4 immediately after the existing `ux-heuristics-lens.md` paragraph. The QA-accelerated path stays unchanged, as it is for the UX lens.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/visual-review/ai-design-tells-lens.md` — new criteria-only lens
- `plugin/skills/visual-review/page-mode.md` — Step 4: apply the new lens after the UX heuristics lens
- `plugin/skills/visual-review/SKILL.md` — Page mode bullet names the new lens
- `docs/plugin-structure.md` — visual-review sub-file row lists `ai-design-tells-lens.md`
- `plugin/skills/visual-review/ux-heuristics-lens.md` — reference only, the structural model

## Gotchas

- Stay scoped to named AI-generated tells. Usability belongs to `ux-heuristics-lens.md` and overall quality to Impeccable, so a row that duplicates either should be cut or reframed as a tell.
- Check `page-mode.md`'s size against any byte ceiling a conformance test pins before adding the paragraph. The lens content itself belongs in the new file, not in `page-mode.md`.
- Some rows (inconsistent spacing, buzzwords) are judgment calls. Mark them rather than implying the whole list is mechanically detectable.

## Original request

Add an AI-generated-design-tells checklist

Current State:
- Two reels independently describe the same problem: AI-generated app/website design is instantly recognizable and forgettable because it converges on the same visual tells.
- Reel DcrqbqZRVvC (transcribed) lists the specific tells: purple-to-blue gradients, gradient hero text, emoji in headings, glassmorphism cards, low-contrast dark mode, three-icon-boxes-in-a-row layouts, badge-above-headline, Lucide icons everywhere, untouched shadcn components, scroll-triggered fade-ins, cursor-following elements, hover-fade buttons, inconsistent spacing, em-dashes everywhere, generic buzzwords, serif-italic accent words, the Space Grotesque + Instrument Serif font pairing, and grain texture overlays.
- A second reel (DcjAVGRBmSC, from Showit) makes the same point in narrative form: "gradient blobs, circle icons, bento grids, fake testimonials" — same theme, folded in here rather than filed as a separate issue.

Deliverables:
- Add a "does this look AI-generated" checklist to claude-tweaks (a design/finish-review lens) listing the specific tells above, for use as a pre-ship pass on any generated UI.
- Frame the fix per the source material: swap generic patterns for real photos/numbers/copy specific to the actual product, not more design polish.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Checklist enumerates at least the tells listed above.
- Running it against a sample AI-generated UI flags at least one applicable item.
