Surface: infra

## Current State

`plugin/skills/dispatch/task-prompt.md` carries the identical "Foreground execution (required)" paragraph verbatim in two places (lines 74-78 and 176-180, one per two-call task-prompt template): "run `npm test` and every other long-running command in the foreground of this turn ... never with `run_in_background`. Never end this turn waiting on a background test run, fix-round, or child agent's completion notification; a dispatched agent that yields this way is never re-woken and the run stalls silently (#1965)."

This wording does not distinguish shell-level `run_in_background` (a genuine headless-stall risk — a dispatched agent's own top-level turn ending with nothing pending to resume it) from the `Agent` tool's own built-in async notification mechanism, which `plugin/skills/_shared/dispatch-waiting.md` documents as the plugin's normal, relied-upon operating mode: "The task-notification that arrives when a dispatched agent finishes is the **primary resume signal** — it is what actually wakes the dispatcher... after dispatching a wave of parallel agents, let their completion notifications drive the next turn." `plugin/skills/review/step3-lens-dispatch.md`'s Low-tier single-read dispatch (line 48) explicitly dispatches one `Agent` per in-scope lens (3b, 3c) at `low` tier and depends on this exact notification mechanism to resume review Step 3.

During a `review,polish,wrap-up` dispatch call (record #2436), Step 3's low-tier single-read lens dispatch launched two async `Agent` tool calls (lens 3b and 3c). Reading task-prompt.md's foreground-execution clause literally as also covering the `Agent` tool's built-in notification (not just shell `run_in_background`), the reviewing session performed the same 3b/3c analysis synchronously in the main thread as a hedge — duplicating work Step 3's own contract already handles asynchronously. Both dispatched agents then returned their completion notifications reliably, within the same turn sequence, moments later — the hedge was unnecessary in this instance, but the ambiguity that caused it is structural, not a one-off misreading.

## Deliverables

1. Rewrite `task-prompt.md`'s "Foreground execution (required)" paragraph (both occurrences, lines 74-78 and 176-180) to explicitly scope the "never end this turn waiting on a ... child agent's completion notification" clause to the case it actually targets: THIS dispatched session's own top-level turn ending with nothing else pending to resume it (the genuine stall risk `#1965` names).
2. Explicitly distinguish that stall risk from an in-turn `Agent`-tool dispatch (a lens-dispatch fan-out, a reproduction pair) whose completion notification the harness is expected to deliver back into the same ongoing turn sequence — cite `_shared/dispatch-waiting.md`'s existing convention rather than restating it, per this repo's degrade-clause/convention-citation discipline (`plan-authoring-checks.md`'s Degrade-clause convention check applies the same discipline to this kind of citation).
3. Confirm the clarified wording does not weaken the original stall-risk warning for genuine shell `run_in_background` usage — the fix narrows the clause's scope, it does not remove the warning.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `task-prompt.md`'s foreground-execution paragraph, in both occurrences, no longer reads as prohibiting an in-turn `Agent`-tool dispatch whose notification is expected to resume the same turn sequence (e.g. `step3-lens-dispatch.md`'s low-tier single-read `Agent` dispatch).
- The clarified wording still unambiguously prohibits shell `run_in_background` for `npm test` and other long-running commands, and still warns against a dispatched session ending its own top-level turn with nothing pending (the `#1965` stall risk) — no regression on the original warning's coverage.
- The clarified wording cites `_shared/dispatch-waiting.md`'s existing "primary resume signal" convention rather than re-deriving or restating it inline.
- A future headless `/flow review,polish,wrap-up` dispatch call can launch Step 3's lens-dispatch `Agent` calls (per `step3-lens-dispatch.md`'s Low-tier single-read dispatch) without a reviewing session needing to guess whether doing so risks a silent stall.
- Both occurrences of the paragraph in `task-prompt.md` stay byte-identical to each other after the edit (matching the file's existing convention of two verbatim copies, one per call template) — a fix landed in only one occurrence would leave the ambiguity live in the other call's prompt.
- `npm test` passes in full after the change (including any conformance test pinning this paragraph's text, if one exists).

## Release Note

Clarified the dispatch prompt's warning about waiting on background work.

## Technical Approach

Edit `task-prompt.md`'s foreground-execution paragraph at both line ranges (74-78, 176-180) identically, narrowing the "never end this turn waiting on ... a child agent's completion notification" clause to name explicitly what it means: a dispatched session's own top-level turn ending with nothing else pending — the scenario `#1965` documents, where the dispatcher session itself never gets re-woken. Add an explicit carve-out or clarifying clause naming the in-turn `Agent`-tool dispatch case as the normal, expected pattern, with a citation to `_shared/dispatch-waiting.md`'s "primary resume signal" convention (its existing text already states the plugin's general position — this task-prompt.md paragraph should point at it, not duplicate it).

Grep the repo for any conformance test asserting on this exact paragraph's text (a byte-pinned prose test, per `skill-prose-conformance-tests`'s convention) before editing, so the fix updates any pinned fixture in the same change rather than leaving a test red.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/dispatch/task-prompt.md` — both occurrences of the "Foreground execution (required)" paragraph (lines 74-78 and 176-180), edited identically.
- `plugin/skills/_shared/dispatch-waiting.md` — cited, not restated; confirm its "primary resume signal" language is still an accurate citation target after this edit (no change expected to this file itself).
- `plugin/skills/review/step3-lens-dispatch.md` — read (not necessarily edited) to confirm the Low-tier single-read dispatch's own wording doesn't also need a matching clarification; if it independently references the same foreground-execution ambiguity, extend the fix there too.
- Any `tests/` file byte-pinning `task-prompt.md`'s foreground-execution paragraph text — update alongside the prose change if one exists.

## Gotchas

- The two occurrences of this paragraph in `task-prompt.md` must stay byte-identical after the edit, per the file's own convention (one copy per two-call template) — editing only one leaves the ambiguity live in whichever call's prompt wasn't fixed.
- Narrowing the clause's scope must not accidentally loosen the genuine shell-`run_in_background` prohibition or the `#1965` stall-risk warning — the fix is a clarification of scope, not a relaxation of the underlying rule.
- This record originated as a "tangential" reflect-light finding (`Origin: reflect light from #2436`), observed once with the hedge turning out to be unnecessary in that instance — the underlying ambiguity is still structural and worth fixing even though the one observed incident cost only a duplicated analysis, not a real stall.

Surface: infra

## Current State

Prose-correcting Claude (asking it to fix a bad response by describing the correction) burns tokens and leaves the bad version in conversation history; Claude Code's `/rewind` command undoes to a prior state at no token cost, but claude-tweaks' own skill/doc guidance never mentions it as the preferred alternative to a prose-based correction. A search of `plugin/` and `docs/` confirms no existing "session hygiene" section or `/rewind` mention exists anywhere in this repo's own guidance.

## Deliverables

Add a brief `/rewind`-over-prose-correction recommendation to the most relevant existing guidance location — likely root `CLAUDE.md`'s Working Approach section (which already covers how to execute tasks generally) or a skill whose scope already touches session-level hygiene/recovery, rather than inventing a new standalone doc for one short tip.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The recommendation is added in one clear, findable location (not duplicated across multiple files) and states the concrete guidance: when a response needs correcting, prefer `/rewind` over a prose-described fix, since it undoes at no token cost and doesn't leave the bad version in history.
- The addition is brief — a few sentences, consistent with `docs/skill-authoring.md`'s general conciseness conventions (this repo already has a documented preference against verbose additions, per the CLAUDE.md conciseness pattern observed elsewhere in this session's own shaping work).

## Release Note

Added guidance to prefer rewinding a session over correcting it in prose.

## Technical Approach

Confirm the best home before writing: check root `CLAUDE.md`'s existing sections (Working Approach is the most likely fit, since it already governs how tasks get executed) against any skill whose scope more specifically covers session-level correction/recovery patterns. Add the recommendation as a short addition to whichever location is the better fit — do not create a new file or section for a tip this size.

### Key Files

- `CLAUDE.md` — most likely location (Working Approach section), pending confirmation against any more specific existing home

## Gotchas

- This is a small, low-risk documentation addition — resist the temptation to expand it into a broader "session hygiene" guide beyond the one concrete recommendation the record asks for. A few sentences is the right size.
- Confirm `/rewind` is indeed the currently correct Claude Code command name before writing it into guidance — platform command names can change across versions, and stale guidance naming a renamed/removed command would be worse than no guidance.

## Original request

Recommend /rewind over prose corrections in session hygiene guidance

Context: Prose-correcting Claude burns tokens and leaves the bad version in history; /rewind undoes at no cost but claude-tweaks never mentions it.

Scope: Add a /rewind recommendation to the relevant lifecycle skill(s).

Surface: infra

## Current State

claude-tweaks' skills and CLAUDE.md guidance encode verification/self-check instructions written for older Claude model defaults. Anthropic's own April 23, 2026 postmortem documents that reasoning-effort defaults, response-length system-prompt instructions, and idle-session context-clearing behavior all swing coding quality independent of model weights — and that its own upgrade guidance for newer, higher-effort models is to remove old verification instructions rather than add more, since new models can over-verify and burn extra turns when stale instructions remain. No current claude-tweaks process re-checks skill/CLAUDE.md verification instructions when the underlying Claude model version changes.

## Deliverables

- A checklist step that, on a tracked model version bump, reviews existing verification/self-check instructions in skills and CLAUDE.md for redundancy with the new model's own built-in verification behavior.
- A short reference doc summarizing the effort/verbosity levers (reasoning effort, response-length prompt instructions, idle-session context-clearing) known to swing coding quality independent of model weights.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Running the review after a tracked model bump produces a keep/trim decision for each verification instruction in a sampled skill.
- The reference doc is linked from wherever CLAUDE.md guidance is authored.

## Release Note

Added a checklist for re-auditing verification instructions after a Claude model upgrade.

## Technical Approach

Add the checklist as a new practice referenced from wherever this repo already tracks maintenance practices tied to external events (comparable in shape to a release checklist item, but triggered by a model version bump rather than a code release). The reference doc is a short, standalone `docs/` file summarizing the three named levers (reasoning-effort defaults, response-length instructions, idle-session context-clearing) and citing the Anthropic postmortem as its source; link it from CLAUDE.md's own guidance-authoring section so a future skill author encounters it before adding a new verification instruction.

### Key Files

- `docs/` — new reference doc summarizing the effort/verbosity levers
- `CLAUDE.md` — link to the new reference doc from the guidance-authoring section; add the checklist-step practice reference

## Gotchas

- This creates a recurring, human-triggered practice, not an automated check — a "tracked model version bump" has no mechanized detection point in this repo today, so the checklist step needs a clear trigger (e.g. "run this the next time you update the model reference in CLAUDE.md's Environment section") rather than assuming automation will invoke it.
- Verify the cited Anthropic postmortem's actual content directly (not just via the secondary Medium-article citation) before writing the reference doc, since the reference doc will be treated as authoritative guidance for future skill authors.

## Original request

Add a practice: re-audit verification prompts on Claude model bumps

Current State:
- claude-tweaks' skills and CLAUDE.md guidance encode verification/self-check instructions written for older Claude model defaults.
- Anthropic's own April 23, 2026 postmortem (cited in the sourced article, with a full reader-proxy fetch confirming the citation) documents that reasoning-effort defaults, response-length system-prompt instructions, and idle-session context-clearing behavior all swing coding quality independent of model weights -- and that its own upgrade guidance for newer, higher-effort models is to remove old verification instructions rather than add more, since new models can over-verify and burn extra turns when stale instructions remain.
- No current claude-tweaks process re-checks skill/CLAUDE.md verification instructions when the underlying Claude model version changes.

Deliverables:
- A checklist step that, on a tracked model version bump, reviews existing verification/self-check instructions in skills and CLAUDE.md for redundancy with the new model's own built-in verification behavior.
- A short reference doc summarizing the effort/verbosity levers (reasoning effort, response-length prompt instructions, idle-session context-clearing) known to swing coding quality independent of model weights.

Acceptance Criteria:

Surface: infra

## Current State

Claude Code reads `AGENTS.md` only when `CLAUDE.md` is missing, so file ordering can silently determine which instructions actually govern a session. Neither `/claude-tweaks:init` nor `/claude-tweaks:harness-health` currently checks for this — a project could have both files present with `AGENTS.md` silently winning (or a stale `AGENTS.md` shadowing an intentionally-maintained `CLAUDE.md`), and nothing in the plugin would surface it. Confirmed: neither `plugin/skills/init/SKILL.md` nor `plugin/skills/harness-health/SKILL.md` currently mentions `AGENTS.md` at all.

## Deliverables

Have `/claude-tweaks:init` and/or `/claude-tweaks:harness-health` detect when both `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md` are present in a project root and warn — naming which file Claude Code actually reads in that configuration, so a maintainer isn't silently governed by the wrong file.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Running `/claude-tweaks:init` (re-run/drift-detection mode) or `/claude-tweaks:harness-health` against a project with both `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md` present produces an explicit warning naming the precedence (`AGENTS.md` is ignored while `CLAUDE.md` exists) and pointing at both files.
- A project with only `CLAUDE.md` (the common case) triggers no such warning — the check is presence-of-both-gated, not a general nag.
- The warning text itself states the actual Claude Code precedence rule (CLAUDE.md wins when both exist) so a reader doesn't have to look it up elsewhere.

## Release Note

Added a warning when a project has both CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md, naming which one Claude Code actually reads.

## Technical Approach

Add a file-presence check (`fs.existsSync` for both `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md` at the project root) to whichever of `/claude-tweaks:init`'s drift-detection pass or `/claude-tweaks:harness-health`'s workflow is the better fit — `harness-health` is likely the more natural home since it already exists to detect harness/config drift, but confirm against each skill's current scope before choosing. Render the warning inline with that skill's existing finding format, not as a new separate mechanism.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/harness-health/SKILL.md` — likely home for the new detection check (confirm against `init/SKILL.md`'s own scope first)
- `plugin/skills/init/SKILL.md` — alternate/complementary home, particularly for the drift-detection re-run path

## Gotchas

- Don't over-warn: a project intentionally maintaining both files for some other tool's benefit (not Claude Code) with `CLAUDE.md` correctly taking precedence is not itself a problem — the warning's job is surfacing the *ambiguity risk*, not asserting both-files-present is always wrong. Keep the tone informational, not an error.
- Confirm the actual current Claude Code precedence rule (CLAUDE.md wins when present, AGENTS.md read only when CLAUDE.md is absent) against current platform behavior before hardcoding it in the warning text — platform behavior can change across Claude Code versions.

## Original request

Verify claude-tweaks setups aren't silently switched off by AGENTS.md

Context: Claude Code reads AGENTS.md only when CLAUDE.md is missing, so file ordering can silently determine which instructions actually govern a session.

Scope: Have init/harness-health detect and warn when both files are present.

groups.body:
Surface: infra

## Current State

Claude Code v2.1.283 shipped a built-in `/doctor` prompt-audit that overlaps with `/claude-tweaks:harness-health`'s own drift checks (`plugin/skills/harness-health/SKILL.md`'s Workflow section documents this skill's checks). Whether the overlap is redundant, complementary, or covers genuinely different ground has not been investigated — this record exists to make that determination and act on it, not to assume the answer either way.

## Deliverables

Investigate what Claude Code's built-in `/doctor` prompt-audit actually checks (via its own documentation/help output) and compare it against `harness-health/SKILL.md`'s documented checks. Decide one of two outcomes and implement it:
1. If the built-in audit genuinely subsumes part of harness-health's scope, have harness-health invoke or defer to it for that overlapping portion rather than duplicating the check.
2. If the overlap is only superficial (different depth, different trigger conditions, or different failure modes caught), explicitly document in `harness-health/SKILL.md` why the two checks stay separate, so a future reader doesn't re-raise the same "isn't this redundant now?" question without the answer already being on record.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `harness-health/SKILL.md` (or a linked doc) states explicitly, after this investigation, either how it now calls/defers to the built-in `/doctor` audit for the overlapping portion, or why it deliberately does not.
- The decision is grounded in an actual comparison of what each check covers, not an assumption — cite the specific check(s) on each side that were compared.

## Release Note

Aligned the harness health check with Claude Code's built-in prompt audit so the two no longer overlap.

## Technical Approach

Run or inspect Claude Code's built-in `/doctor` command (via `--help`, its own output, or release notes for v2.1.283) to determine its actual check coverage. Cross-reference against `harness-health/SKILL.md`'s Workflow section (checks currently documented there) to find genuine overlap versus superficial similarity. The decision itself (defer vs. document-separation) follows directly from what that comparison finds — this record's Deliverables intentionally don't presuppose which outcome is correct.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/harness-health/SKILL.md` — the Workflow section documenting current checks; the target for either the defer-call or the explicit separation-rationale

## Gotchas

- Don't assume redundancy or non-redundancy without actually running/inspecting the built-in `/doctor` audit first — the capture that filed this record only noted the overlap exists, not which way it resolves.
- If harness-health ends up deferring part of its scope to a built-in Claude Code command, confirm that command is stable/versioned enough to depend on (Claude Code version drift is a real risk for a plugin-level dependency on harness-internal tooling) before wiring it in as a hard dependency.

## Original request

Reconcile harness-health with Claude Code's built-in prompt-audit

Context: Claude Code v2.1.283 shipped a built-in /doctor prompt-audit that overlaps with harness-health's own drift checks.

Scope: Decide whether harness-health should call the built-in audit or explicitly document why it stays separate.

groups.body:
Surface: infra

**Related:** #2806 (untangle verify/args.js parseArgs — both records edit `plugin/bin/lib/verify/args.js`; build order matters, coordinate before dispatching both)

## Current State

`verify.js --cmd <name>=<command>` spawns each check's command via a child shell with no way to set an environment variable for just that one check's process, portably across platforms.

A caller of `verify.js` needs to set an environment variable for one named check's spawned process only (e.g. to gate an optional/expensive code path off for that check). On Windows the runner spawns via `cmd.exe`, so a POSIX-style `VAR=val command` prefix inside the `--cmd` value fails outright (`'VAR' is not recognized as an internal or external command`). The only workaround found was writing a throwaway wrapper script (a `.bat` file on Windows: `set VAR=val` then the real command) instead of passing the env var inline to `--cmd`.

## Deliverables

A repeatable `--cmd-env <check-name>=<KEY=VALUE>` flag that sets environment variables for that named check's spawned process via the child_process `env` option (not shell syntax) — works identically across `cmd.exe` and POSIX shells, with no wrapper script needed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `verify.js --cmd foo="node check.js" --cmd-env foo=MY_VAR=1` spawns `foo`'s process with `MY_VAR=1` set in its environment, verified cross-platform (or, if only one platform is available to test on, verified via the child_process `env` option's documented behavior rather than shell-syntax parsing).
- A `--cmd-env` naming a check not declared via `--cmd` produces the same class of clear error `verify.js` already gives for other `--cmd`-name mismatches (per the existing `--cmd-name-vs-declaration` check noted in `bin/verify.js`).
- Omitting `--cmd-env` entirely leaves existing `--cmd`-only invocations unaffected (backward compatible, no behavior change for callers not using the new flag).
- `npm test` passes in full after the change.

## Release Note

Added a way to pass environment variables to verification checks that works the same on Windows and POSIX shells.

## Technical Approach

Add `--cmd-env` parsing to `plugin/bin/lib/verify/args.js` alongside the existing `--cmd` parsing, validating the `<check-name>=<KEY=VALUE>` shape and cross-checking the named check exists among declared `--cmd` names (mirroring the existing name-vs-declaration validation noted at `bin/verify.js`'s AC5/L13 comment). Thread the resolved per-check env map through to wherever the spawn actually happens (likely `plugin/bin/lib/verify/run.js`), merging it into the child_process `env` option for that check's spawn call only — not via shell-syntax prefixing, which is what breaks under `cmd.exe`.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/verify/args.js` — add `--cmd-env` flag parsing and validation
- `plugin/bin/lib/verify/run.js` — thread the per-check env map into the spawn call's `env` option
- `plugin/bin/verify.js` — the CLI entrypoint documenting available flags

## Gotchas

- Must use child_process's `env` option, not a shell-syntax `VAR=val` prefix — that's precisely the cross-platform failure this record exists to fix, so reintroducing shell-syntax passthrough anywhere in the implementation would not actually solve the problem.
- The per-check env map should merge with (not replace) the spawned process's inherited environment, unless there's an existing `verify.js` convention for env isolation that says otherwise — check current spawn behavior before assuming.

## Original request

**Summary:** `verify.js --cmd <name>=<command>` spawns each check's command via a child shell with no way to set an environment variable for just that one check's process, portably across platforms.

**Kind:** Gap

**Affected component:** bin/verify.js

**Use case:** A caller of `verify.js` needs to set an environment variable for one named check's spawned process only (e.g. to gate an optional/expensive code path off for that check). On Windows the runner spawns via `cmd.exe`, so a POSIX-style `VAR=val command` prefix inside the `--cmd` value fails outright (`'VAR' is not recognized as an internal or external command`). The only workaround found was writing a throwaway wrapper script (a `.bat` file on Windows: `set VAR=val` then the real command) instead of passing the env var inline to `--cmd`.

**Definition:** Clear — a `--cmd-env <check-name>=<KEY=VALUE>` flag (repeatable) that sets environment variables for that named check's spawned process via the child_process `env` option (not shell syntax) would work identically across `cmd.exe` and POSIX shells, with no wrapper script needed.

**Plugin version:** 6.129.0

---

groups.body:
Surface: infra

**Related:** #2746, #2748 (same shape — pure verification-and-close findings, already-resolved by the time of shaping)

## Current State

**Both bundled defects in this report are already fixed — verified against the current codebase during shaping, not just claimed.**

**Defect (2), the `impeccable-cli` pin:** the report claims the pin is `3.6.0` versus an installed `4.1.0`. Read `plugin/skills/design-wrapper/impeccable-cli.md`'s actual header: `<!-- upstream-pin: impeccable-cli@4.1.0 -->` — the pin is already `4.1.0`, matching the filer's own installed version. Whatever prompted this filing, the pin has since been bumped (the file's own prose even documents a prior stale-pin incident, `[IL-89]`, and treats pin currency carefully) — nothing to fix here anymore.

**Defect (1), `verify.js --changed-files` returning an empty set:** read `plugin/bin/lib/verify/changed-files.js`'s `resolveBase` function directly. It already implements exactly the fix this report asks for, tracked as `#2486`: "a stamp anchor identical to HEAD answers 'nothing since the last full verify'... but a caller that explicitly named `--integration-branch` is asking a different question... When the anchor is this degenerate and an integration branch was given, skip it and fall through to the integration-branch resolution below." `bin/verify.js`'s `changedFilesMode` (the actual `--changed-files` call site) already passes `requireNonDegenerate: true`, triggering this fallback. It even goes further than the report's own ask: if the resolved base *still* equals HEAD after the fallback (a genuinely merged branch, or no `--integration-branch` given), it emits an explicit `result.warning = 'resolved base equals HEAD — diff will be empty'` in the JSON output — turning the silent-empty-set trap the filer hit into a clearly signaled condition rather than a fix that could itself regress silently.

The filer's plugin version (6.126.0) predates the currently-installed 6.129.0 — both fixes evidently shipped in that gap. This record, as originally filed, has no remaining buildable work.

## Deliverables

- Confirm both fixes are present and correct on the branch/version the build actually runs against (re-read `impeccable-cli.md`'s pin and `changed-files.js`'s `resolveBase`/`changedFilesMode` fresh — don't just trust this shaping pass's snapshot, since more time may have passed).
- Close this record with a comment citing the confirming evidence (the pin's current value, `#2486`'s `requireNonDegenerate` mechanism and the `result.warning` field) — no code change.
- If re-verification finds either fix is NOT actually present on the branch this builds against (a genuine surprise, contradicting this shaping pass's findings), stop and report that discrepancy explicitly rather than assuming this record's premise-correction was wrong — that would itself be worth investigating.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A fresh read of `impeccable-cli.md`'s pin comment and `changed-files.js`'s `resolveBase`/`changedFilesMode` confirms both fixes are present (or the build reports a genuine contradiction, if found).
- The record is closed with a comment stating why, not left open or silently abandoned.
- No production code changes are expected; `npm test` passes regardless (no test-affecting change).

## Release Note

Fixed changed-file detection returning nothing when the verification stamp is at the latest commit.

## Technical Approach

This is a verify-and-close record, not a code-change record — the "build" here is re-confirming what this shaping pass already found and then closing the issue with that evidence cited, per this codebase's own `Close (GitHub)` convention (comment first, always — never a silent close).

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/design-wrapper/impeccable-cli.md` — the pin comment to re-confirm (`4.1.0`)
- `plugin/bin/lib/verify/changed-files.js` — `resolveBase`'s `#2486` degenerate-anchor fallback to re-confirm
- `plugin/bin/verify.js` — `changedFilesMode`'s `requireNonDegenerate: true` call and its `result.warning` field to re-confirm

## Gotchas

- Don't assume this record is simply wrong to have been filed — it was accurate for the filer's plugin version (6.126.0) at the time; the fixes evidently shipped afterward. This is a normal case of feedback lagging the fix, not a bad report.
- If closing this record, the closing comment should name the specific commit/version where each fix landed if that's discoverable (e.g. via `git log` on the two files), giving the filer's project a concrete upgrade target — worth a quick check at build time, not required if not cheaply discoverable.

## Original request

Upstream defect report — `verify.js --changed-files` returns an empty set when the runner stamp sits at HEAD; `impeccable-cli` pin 3.6.0 vs installed 4.1.0

Component: `bin/verify.js` (`--changed-files`), `skills/test/SKILL.md` pipeline story selection, `skills/design-wrapper/impeccable-cli.md` (pin)
Kind: defect (two related)
Version: claude-tweaks 6.126.0

## Symptom

(1) After Common Step 5 stamped verification at HEAD, `/test`'s pipeline story selection calls `verify.js --changed-files --integration-branch develop`; the runner uses the stamp's own sha as the base, so the changed set is `[]` and the selection rule reads "zero matches → web surface → run the full story set" — the opposite of what the diff warrants. The record's own range (plan commit..HEAD) intersected `source_files` for 4 of 15 stories; the controller had to compute that by hand.
(2) `impeccable-cli.md` pins the CLI at 3.6.0 and states an off-pin CLI fails the contract test, while `npx impeccable --version` resolves 4.1.0 on this machine; `detect --json` still returned the documented array shape, so the gate ran, but a stale pin turns every run into a documented contract breach.

## Expected

(1) `--changed-files` should fall back to the record's materialized range (or `merge-base(integration-branch)..HEAD`) whenever the stamp sha equals HEAD, instead of returning an empty set; the story-selection rule should treat an empty set from that cause as "unknown", not "none". (2) Bump or widen the `impeccable-cli` pin (4.1.x parses identically for `detect --json`).

## Evidence

Origin: consolidated Review Console — run `2026-09-21T213441-spec-2697-2757-2758-2759`; found while executing `flow/multispec-review-console.md`'s Auto-resolution short-circuit against this run's five run directories

Defer-reason: tangential

## Current State

Two defects in `plugin/bin/lib/console/resolve.js`'s `SECTION_MAP`, both observed live on this run's
parent run directory.

### 1. The curation engine's own staged prefixes are not in `SECTION_MAP`

`bin/wrap-up-engine.js`'s `claude-md` and `decision-records` registry rows stage their findings as
`staged/wrap-up-claude-md-{n}.md` and `staged/wrap-up-adr-{n}.md`. Neither prefix appears in
`SECTION_MAP`, so `classifyStagedItem` falls through to its catch-all and the resolver reported:

```
| 5 | Pending review | wrap-up-adr-1.md       | AUTO-RESOLVED: pending | unmapped-prefix |
| 6 | Pending review | wrap-up-claude-md-1.md | AUTO-RESOLVED: pending | unmapped-prefix |
| 7 | Pending review | wrap-up-claude-md-2.md | AUTO-RESOLVED: pending | unmapped-prefix |
```

All three belong in **Configuration updates** — `ENGINE_ROW_SECTIONS` already maps `claude-md` and
`decision-records` to `SECTIONS.CONFIG`, and the console's own "On approval" step 5 says config
updates (CLAUDE.md, rules, ADRs) apply under Approve-all. The engine-row path only emits rows whose
`action` is `applied`, so a `staged` engine finding reaches the console **only** through the
staged-file path — which is exactly the path that does not recognize it.

Consequence: at `unattended`, a `consoleAutoResolve` run silently leaves every engine-staged
CLAUDE.md/Don'ts/ADR proposal unapplied and merges anyway. The `unmapped-prefix` fallback is
fail-safe by design ("a new producer can never slip past the console"), and it did its job here — but
these are not new producers, they are the engine's own, and the mismatch means the curation engine's
`claude-md` and `decision-records` rows are effectively inert under auto-resolution. This run had to
apply all three by hand against the skill's own prose.

### 2. A `.shadow-dup` is not always a duplicate

`SECTION_MAP`'s first row classifies any `*.shadow-dup` as `shadow-dup-collision` with the comment
"is a duplicate of some other staged file, not a proposal of its own." That is a guess, and on this
run it was wrong for 2 of 7: `spec-2758/staged/build-deviation-1.md.shadow-dup` and
`build-deviation-2.md.shadow-dup` hold **different findings** from their anchored namesakes — real
proposals recovered from a clobbering write (see the `stage-item.js` id-allocation record). The other
5 (all in `spec-2757/`) were byte-identical, as the comment assumes.

Resolving to `pending` is the right *stance* either way, so nothing was lost here. The defect is the
stated **reason**: it tells a reader the file is redundant when it may be the only surviving copy of a
finding. `hooks.js sweep-shadow` already computes duplicate-vs-divergence; the resolver throws that
away and re-guesses.

## Deliverables

- Add `wrap-up-claude-md-` and `wrap-up-adr-` to `SECTION_MAP`, both routing to `SECTIONS.CONFIG`.
  Audit every staged prefix the engine and the skill corpus can actually write against the table, and
  add a test that fails when a producer writes a prefix the table does not know.
- Make the `.shadow-dup` row's reason honest: compare against the anchored file (or read
  `sweep-shadow`'s own verdict) and report `shadow-dup-duplicate` vs `shadow-dup-divergent`. A
  divergent copy must read as a real proposal awaiting a human, not as a redundant copy.

## Acceptance Criteria

A run directory containing `wrap-up-claude-md-1.md` and `wrap-up-adr-1.md` resolves them under
Configuration updates with an `approve` resolution, not `pending — unmapped-prefix`. Pinned by a test.

A test walks the producer set (engine row ids plus the skill corpus's staged filenames) against
`SECTION_MAP` and fails on any prefix with no row — so the next producer added cannot reintroduce
this.

Given one byte-identical and one divergent `.shadow-dup` beside their anchors, the resolver reports
two distinguishable reasons.

_Filed by the consolidated Review Console (`flow/multispec-review-console.md`)._

## Release Note

Fixed unattended Review Consoles silently skipping staged CLAUDE.md and decision-record proposals.

Origin: consolidated Review Console — run `2026-09-21T213441-spec-2697-2757-2758-2759`, ledger row #20 (residual scope; the reflect finding's plan-level half was already applied as a skill update at `301a7351b`)

Defer-reason: genuinely-larger

## Current State

Adding a flag to a skill requires updating every *syntactic mirror* of that skill's argument surface.
The count of those mirrors is currently carried in a plan author's head, and it has been wrong twice:

- **#679** established "a new flag has exactly two syntactic-mirror surfaces beyond the Input table"
  — the `argument-hint` frontmatter line and the Input parse line.
- **#2759** proved that convention was itself an undercount. Task 3 updated both named surfaces;
  Task 6's full-suite gate then found a **third**: `plugin/skills/help/reference-card.md`'s `Takes`
  column, byte-pinned by `tests/reference-card-argument-hint.test.js` under #564. Fixed at `613e230`.

It was caught only by luck of two coincidences: that a byte-pinning suite happened to exist for that
particular surface, and that the run's gate compared failing-file **sets** per file rather than
totals (346 failures against a 395 baseline reads as an improvement; only the per-file diff exposed
the new red file).

The plan-authoring half of the fix has shipped: `plugin/skills/build/plan-authoring-checks.md` now
carries "Derive a flag's mirror surfaces by grepping for an existing flag rather than from a
remembered count" (applied this run at `301a7351b`). That makes the next plan author less likely to
undercount. It does **not** make the enumeration canonical, and it does not make an undercount
detectable — which is the residual this record covers.

## Deliverables

- One canonical enumeration of every `argument-hint` mirror surface — a named table in
  `docs/skill-authoring.md`, or a new `plugin/skills/_shared/argument-hint-mirrors.md` — listing the
  frontmatter line, the Input parse line, and `help/reference-card.md`'s `Takes` column as permanent
  entries, with room for the next one.
- One conformance test that walks that enumeration **mechanically** for every skill, so a skill whose
  flag set disagrees across surfaces fails by construction rather than by whichever byte-pin happens
  to exist.
- Retire the "exactly two surfaces" wording wherever it still appears.

## Acceptance Criteria

Adding a flag to any skill's `argument-hint` and leaving `help/reference-card.md`'s `Takes` column
stale fails the new conformance test — proven by making that exact change and showing the test red,
then green after the mirror is updated.

The enumeration lives in exactly one file; no other file restates the list (this repo's
Cross-references convention).

Every existing skill passes the new test at the time it lands, or the exceptions are named.

_Filed by the consolidated Review Console (`flow/multispec-review-console.md`), from
`spec-2759/staged/reflect-1.md`._

## Release Note

Made the list of places a skill's argument hint must match canonical and checked automatically.

Origin: consolidated Review Console — run `2026-09-21T213441-spec-2697-2757-2758-2759`, ledger row #31

Defer-reason: genuinely-larger

## Current State

**`bin/stage-item.js` silently destroyed two staged Review Console proposals in this run.** The
filename counter that allocates `build-deviation-{n}` restarts **per writer**, not per run
directory, so a later writer in the same `spec-{N}/staged/` reuses `build-deviation-1` /
`build-deviation-2` and overwrites whatever an earlier writer had already put there.

Concretely, in `spec-2758/staged/`:

| Written | File | Content |
|---|---|---|
| 07:59:24 | `build-deviation-1.md` | agent-browser -> playwright-cli tooling premise correction |
| 07:59:24 | `build-deviation-2.md` | inline Interaction-style directive (forbidden since #1909) |
| 11:13 | `build-deviation-1.md` | skill-graph reverse-edge deviation — **overwrote the 07:59 file** |
| 11:13 | `build-deviation-2.md` | AC7 no-running-app deviation — **overwrote the 07:59 file** |

`spec-2758/decisions.md` records all four `STAGED` lines under those two names, so the audit trail
said four proposals existed while the directory held two. The consolidated Review Console reads
`staged/` — it would have rendered **3** items for #2758 instead of the real **5**, and the two lost
findings would never have reached a human.

They survived only because a worktree shadow copy existed; `hooks.js sweep-shadow` recovered them
non-destructively as `build-deviation-1.md.shadow-dup` / `build-deviation-2.md.shadow-dup`. That is
luck, not a mechanism — the same sweep found 7 collisions across the run, 5 of them (all in
`spec-2757/`) byte-identical and harmless, and exactly these 2 divergent.

This is silent data loss in a sanctioned run-directory writer whose entire job is to make a proposal
durable until a human sees it.

## Deliverables

- Allocate staged-item ids against the **target run directory's existing contents**, not against
  per-writer state: read `staged/` and pick the next free `{kind}-{n}`.
- Make a collision impossible to lose silently regardless: refuse to overwrite an existing
  `staged/{name}` (non-zero exit with the existing path named), or write to the next free suffix and
  report the adjusted name on stdout. Never a blind clobber.
- Audit the other sanctioned run-dir writers (`log-decision.js`, `set-config.js`) for the same
  per-writer-state assumption.

## Acceptance Criteria

Two `stage-item.js` invocations from different processes, staging the same `--id` kind into the same
run directory, produce **two** files; neither is lost. Pinned by a regression test that fails against
the current allocator.

An attempted overwrite of an existing `staged/{name}` is a reported outcome (non-zero exit, or a
renamed write echoed on stdout), never a silent success.

`hooks.js sweep-shadow`'s collision report distinguishes duplicate from divergence, as it did here —
keep that, but it must stop being the only thing standing between a proposal and the void.

_Filed by the consolidated Review Console (`flow/multispec-review-console.md`)._

## Release Note

Fixed staged Review Console proposals being silently overwritten when two writers picked the same name.

Origin: consolidated Review Console — run `2026-09-21T213441-spec-2697-2757-2758-2759`, ledger row #17 (`deferred`; the row promised a staged Queue-write proposal that was never written — filed here at the console instead)

Defer-reason: genuinely-larger

## Current State

`plugin/bin/lib/gif/palette.js` was rewritten during #2758's fix wave (`41dc8424f`) to fix an
earlier pathology (224 s / 900 MB RSS on one real walkthrough) using distinct-colour dedup plus a
cached nearest-index lookup. The re-review then measured what the rewrite actually made it bound by:
**distinct colour count, not pixel count.**

| Input | quantize | RSS |
|---|---|---|
| real 1280x720 UI screenshots (the shipped fixtures) | 58 ms | — |
| adversarial 8-frame 1280x720 gradient + noise, 259,895 distinct colours | **482,135 ms** | **1,336 MB** |

That adversarial figure is worse than the original bug it replaced. UI screenshots sit in the fast
band (low thousands to tens of thousands of distinct colours), so `/claude-tweaks:walkthrough` over
an ordinary app is fine; a walkthrough over a photo-, map-, or video-heavy page falls off the cliff.

The shipped perf regression test does not bound this case: it runs at 400x300 against a <5000 ms
budget and measures 730 ms — entirely inside the fast band, so it can never go red for the failure
mode above.

## Deliverables

A colour-count-bounded quantizer path — sampling, pre-bucketing, or an explicit distinct-colour cap
that degrades quality instead of time — so wall-clock and RSS stay bounded regardless of input
entropy. Plus a perf test that actually exercises the slow band (a high-distinct-colour fixture), not
only the fast one.

## Acceptance Criteria

The adversarial case above (8 frames, 1280x720, ~260k distinct colours) completes within a stated
wall-clock and RSS budget — quote the measured numbers before and after.

A committed perf test covers the high-distinct-colour band and is proven to go red against the
pre-fix quantizer.

The real-screenshot fast band does not regress (still ~tens of ms at 1280x720).

_Filed by the consolidated Review Console (`flow/multispec-review-console.md`). Ledger row #17
recorded this as "staged as a backlog candidate for the Wrap-Up Review Console's Queue writes", but
no staged file was ever written to `spec-2758/staged/` — the console found the gap and filed the
record directly rather than letting the row close with nothing behind it._

## Release Note

Bounded GIF encoding time and memory on high-detail walkthrough recordings.

Origin: ledger resolve gate (Phase 2, `ledgerRouteRemainder`) — run `2026-09-21T213441-spec-2697-2757-2758-2759`, ledger row #18 (as corrected by row #28)

Defer-reason: pre-existing-outside-diff

## Current State

`tests/bin-lib/skill-audit/context-cost.test.js`'s composed-bytes ceiling check is red on the
integration branch:

```
worktree-setup @ build\SKILL.md:170: 45.5 KB > 45.0 KB
```

Root cause is traced, not guessed: the breach arrived with commit `522f8b6d1` (record #2348).
`git merge-base --is-ancestor 522f8b6d1 c3a0057f0` exits 0, so it is an ancestor of this run's own
base and predates every commit in this run. #2758's only edit to that test file was an unrelated
description-char-ceiling bump.

A composed-call-site budget that is already over its ceiling cannot report a *new* breach — it is
permanently red, so the next caller to push `build/SKILL.md`'s composed cost up gets no signal at
all. That is the real cost: the check has stopped being a guard.

**Scope correction (important for whoever picks this up).** Ledger row #18 originally bundled a
second claim — that `tests/demo-visual-decision-adoption.test.js` was a regression from #2697's
`b8fd015d9`. The run's batch-reflect pass disproved that: it is a bare-LF-literal-against-a-CRLF-read
failure, reproducible on an unmodified checkout, and `b8fd015d9` never touched
`docs/skill-graph.md`. That half is tracked with the other three instances of its class on its own
record and is **not** in scope here. The mis-attribution itself is recorded as `[IL-160]`.

## Deliverables

Bring `worktree-setup`'s composed cost at `build/SKILL.md:170` back under the 45.0 KB ceiling, or
move the ceiling deliberately with a stated reason — whichever is the honest answer after reading
what `522f8b6d1` added. A split of the composed set, a lazy-load of one member, or a documented
ceiling raise are all acceptable; silently widening the threshold to make the suite green is not.

## Acceptance Criteria

`node --test tests/bin-lib/skill-audit/context-cost.test.js` passes on the integration branch, with
the `worktree-setup @ build/SKILL.md:170` call site reported under its ceiling — quote the measured
before/after byte counts.

If the ceiling was raised rather than the cost reduced, `docs/plugin-structure.md`'s budget prose
states the new number and why, so the next reader does not treat the raise as drift.

## Release Note

Brought the worktree setup instructions back under their context-size ceiling so new breaches are reported again.

## Provenance

Routed here by the resolve gate's Phase 2 at this project's `autonomy: unattended` ceiling via the
`ledgerRouteRemainder` bookkeeping capability (`_shared/autonomy-ceiling.md`). Phase 1 fix-exhaust:
not fix-now eligible — the breach originates outside this run's diff, in a commit already on the
integration branch before the run's base, and fixing it means re-budgeting a composed call site that
none of this run's four specs owns. Its blocker reason is `pre-existing-outside-diff`, which
`STRUCTURED_FLOOR` maps to `false`, so `ledgerNarrowing` (`trusted`+) did not cover it;
`ledgerRouteRemainder` (`unattended` only) is the capability that routes that remainder, and it
authorizes exactly one disposition — `Route to a record -> Keep (backlog)`, never `Accept`, `Drop`,
or `Fix anyway`.

Origin: ledger resolve gate

## Current State

`wrap-up/review-console.md`'s Multi-spec defer protocol step 4 instructs writing `{run-dir}/verify-expectations.json` (`{"version":1,"memory":[],"upstream":[],"deferred":[...]}`) into the pipeline run directory. The three sanctioned run-dir writers documented in `gh-api-module-pattern/cli-wrapper-contract.md` — `log-decision.js` (`decisions.md`), `stage-item.js` (`staged/`), `set-config.js` (`config.yml`) — cover exactly three filenames; none covers this one. A direct `Write` to the main-checkout run-dir path from a worktree-isolated per-spec session is refused by the PreToolUse worktree-isolation gate.

Observed twice in the same multi-spec run (2026-09-21T213441-spec-2697-2757-2758-2759): `spec-2758`'s wrap-up hit this gap and logged it as ledger #19 of `docs/plans/2026-09-21-spec-2697-2757-2758-2759-ledger.md`, flagging it for "the run's final wrap-up, which can write it once outside worktree isolation, or a backlog record proposing a fourth sanctioned writer CLI for this file class." `spec-2759`'s wrap-up (the run's actual final spec) re-confirmed the same gap still applies — it is also still a worktree-isolated session, so it cannot write the file either. The bounded consequence (per `review-console.md`): a per-spec `verify` run renders `memory-updates`/`upstream-feedback` as `unknown (expectations file missing)` instead of `skip (nothing recorded)` — accepted, does not block the consolidated Review Console, which reads `decisions.md`/`staged/` directly.

## Deliverables

A fourth sanctioned run-dir writer CLI (or an added mode on an existing one) covering `verify-expectations.json`, following the same `run(argv, deps)` seam, exit-code vocabulary, and run-dir anchoring guard as `log-decision.js`/`stage-item.js`/`set-config.js` (`gh-api-module-pattern`'s CLI wrapper contract).

## Acceptance Criteria

A worktree-isolated `/claude-tweaks:wrap-up` session can write `spec-{n}/verify-expectations.json` (or update it) via the new/extended sanctioned CLI without tripping the PreToolUse worktree-isolation gate — verified by a regression test exercising the CLI from a simulated worktree-isolated context.

`review-console.md`'s per-spec `verify` step no longer needs the `unknown (expectations file missing)` fallback once the file is actually written — the memory-updates/upstream-feedback probe reads `skip (nothing recorded)` normally.

_Filed by `ledger resolve gate` via specShapedBody._

## Release Note

Added a sanctioned way to record verification expectations from a worktree-isolated wrap-up.

Defer-reason: genuinely-larger

## Current State

The prose-conformance suites (`tests/*-conformance*.test.js` and siblings such as `tests/feedback-watermark-prose.test.js`, `tests/demo-*.test.js`) read `plugin/skills/**/*.md` with a raw `fs.readFileSync(..., 'utf8')` and assert on literals, `startsWith(heading + '\n')`, and byte counts. This repo has `core.autocrlf=true` and no `.gitattributes`, so any file git re-checks-out on a Windows box (a revert, a `git checkout`, a fresh clone) carries CRLF in the working copy while files written by an editor or the Write tool stay LF.

Observed on #2697's run: `tests/skill-mode-split-conformance.test.js` was red at HEAD purely because a revert re-checked-out one sub-file (`plugin/skills/demo/follow-up-record.md`, `i/lf w/crlf` per `git ls-files --eol`) — fixed by normalizing `\r\n` in that test's `read()` helper. `tests/feedback-watermark-prose.test.js:190` fails on this machine today for the same reason (`'.claude-tweaks/feedback/\r'`), and the run's pre-flight sweep baseline (342 failures / 103 files, ledger #2 of run 2026-09-21T213441-spec-2697-2757-2758-2759) is dominated by CRLF/path-shaped failures of this class.

## Deliverables

One shared EOL-normalizing read helper for prose-conformance tests (e.g. `tests/helpers/read-skill.js` exporting `readText(rel)` that returns the file with `\r\n` → `\n`), adopted by every `tests/**` suite that reads `plugin/skills/**/*.md`, `docs/**/*.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, or `.gitignore` for literal assertions — replacing each suite's private `fs.readFileSync` read.

OR, if judged cleaner: a committed `.gitattributes` declaring `* text=auto eol=lf` (or `*.md text eol=lf` plus the other asserted text types) so checkouts are LF on every platform — with a one-time renormalization commit (`git add --renormalize .`) and a note in `docs/donts.md` or `CLAUDE.md`'s Commands section about the Windows baseline shrinking. Pick one; state why the other was not chosen.

## Acceptance Criteria

`node --test tests/feedback-watermark-prose.test.js` passes on a Windows checkout with `core.autocrlf=true` (its `.gitignore and step-04 intentionally diverge post-#856` test no longer fails on a trailing `\r`).

A re-checkout of any `plugin/skills/**/*.md` sub-file (e.g. `git checkout -- plugin/skills/demo/follow-up-record.md` on Windows) leaves `tests/skill-mode-split-conformance.test.js` and every other prose-conformance suite green — verified by a re-run after such a checkout on a Windows box, quoted in the wrap-up.

The Windows pre-flight baseline failure count for `node tools/run-tests.js` drops measurably versus the 342-failure baseline recorded on 2026-09-21 (quote before/after counts); failures that remain are named and are not CRLF/EOL-shaped.

_Filed by `ledger resolve gate` via specShapedBody._
---

## Release Note

Fixed prose-checking tests that fail on Windows checkouts with CRLF line endings.

## Amendment at the consolidated Review Console (2026-09-22)

The run's batch-reflect pass found a **fourth** call site of this exact defect class and corrected a
mis-attribution it had already caused. The Deliverables above must name **four** call sites, not two:

| Test | State at filing |
|---|---|
| `tests/skill-mode-split-conformance.test.js` | already fixed in-run (#2697's fix wave normalized its `read()`) — keep as the reference shape |
| `tests/feedback-watermark-prose.test.js:190` | open — the original motivating instance |
| `tests/intake-conformance.test.js:28` | open — bare-LF `SKILL.indexOf('\n\n', tableStart)` against a non-normalized read; proven environmental twice in one run (run ledger #21) |
| `tests/demo-visual-decision-adoption.test.js:208` | open — bare-LF `skillGraph.indexOf('## demo\n')`; the literal resolves only in its CRLF form at offset 42021, so the section slice is empty and the assertion fails regardless of content (run ledger #28) |

The fourth instance was initially mis-attributed (run ledger #18) to commit `b8fd015d9` — #2697's own
demo-mode-split extraction, the one commit on the branch touching `demo/` — and carried into the run
ledger as a real un-fixed regression. It is not: it reproduces on an unmodified checkout, and
`b8fd015d9` never touched `docs/skill-graph.md`. That mis-attribution cost a full root-cause pass and
a second pass to undo, and is recorded separately as `[IL-160]`.

Acceptance is therefore widened: all four files above pass on a Windows checkout with
`core.autocrlf=true` after the change, and the chosen mechanism (shared helper, or the
`.gitattributes` policy) is applied to every `tests/**` suite that reads repo markdown for literal
assertions — not only the four named here.

(ledger rows #3, #21, #28)._

Surface: infra

## Current State
During `#2595`'s `build,test` pipeline run (2026-09-22, plugin 6.126.0), `npm test` reported 6 failing tests out of 9374, in files entirely outside that build's diff (which only touched `plugin/skills/review/step3-lens-dispatch.md`, `plugin/skills/review/step3-debate-and-refutation.md`, and `plugin/skills/_shared/subagent-output-contract.md`). Each failure reproduced consistently when the affected file was re-run in isolation (`node --test {file}`), ruling out machine-load flake per CLAUDE.md's tolerance note. Three distinct root causes across four files:

1. **`tests/impeccable-plugin-contract.test.js`** (3 failures: "the installed plugin matches the pinned version", "gatherSignals() executes cleanly and returns the documented shape", "the CLI entrypoint accepts no flags") — the installed Impeccable plugin resolves to version `4.3.1`, but the test suite's fixtures are pinned to `4.0.2`. The first failure's own error message states the remedy plainly: "Install 4.0.2, or re-pin deliberately by re-recording the fixtures against the new version." The other two failures are downstream of the same unresolved pin (`could not resolve an installed root at the pin`).
2. **`tests/console-execute.test.js`** (1 failure: "reconcile(): the console check is wired in and reachable via ALL_CHECKS on a pr-first project") — assertion "the console check must have run under pr-first" fails; the console check does not appear to be reachable via `ALL_CHECKS` under a `pr-first` integration-model project in this environment.
3. **`tests/bin-lib/visual-decide/cli.test.js`** (1 failure: "stop is stale-PID tolerant (dead PID -> already-stopped, exit 0)") — expects the stop command to treat a dead PID as already-stopped (exit 0); observed `false !== true`, suggesting the stale-PID detection path isn't triggering as expected in this sandbox.
4. **`tests/bin-lib/hooks/reconcile-background.test.js`** (1 failure: "reconcile-background: the same abandoned interrupted run IS archived when CLAUDE_TWEAKS_SESSION_ID is unset (control — unchanged fallback behavior, #1687 AC2)") — expected the original run dir to have been archived away; observed it was not (`true !== false` on "expected the original run dir to have been archived away").

None of these are related to #2595's scope (a documentation-only fix to the review Step 3 `SCRATCH:` dispatch lines and the Scratch rule in `subagent-output-contract.md`).

**Related:** #2531 (`impeccable-plugin-contract.test.js`'s version-pin test failing in a sandbox with a mismatched plugin cache) — same root symptom as this record's Deliverable 1 (Impeccable pin `4.0.2` vs. installed `4.3.1`), filed separately and already `ready`. Check #2531's resolution before duplicating that fix here — see Gotchas.

## Deliverables
1. Either install Impeccable plugin `4.0.2` in the CI/sandbox baseline this repo tests against, or deliberately re-pin `tests/impeccable-plugin-contract.test.js`'s fixtures to the currently-installed `4.3.1` (whichever this repo's maintainer intends as the supported version going forward). **Coordinate with #2531 first** — it targets the identical failure; if #2531 lands first, this deliverable becomes a verification step, not a fix.
2. Diagnose why `console-execute`'s reconcile check is not reachable via `ALL_CHECKS` on a `pr-first` project in this environment, and fix the wiring (or the test, if the wiring is correct and the test's fixture/setup is stale).
3. Diagnose why the stale-PID tolerance test in `tests/bin-lib/visual-decide/cli.test.js` observes `false` where `true` is expected, and fix the stop command or the test.
4. Diagnose why `tests/bin-lib/hooks/reconcile-background.test.js`'s abandoned-interrupted-run archival control case is not archiving as expected, and fix the reconcile-background logic or the test.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `node --test tests/impeccable-plugin-contract.test.js` exits 0.
2. `node --test tests/console-execute.test.js` exits 0.
3. `node --test tests/bin-lib/visual-decide/cli.test.js` exits 0.
4. `node --test tests/bin-lib/hooks/reconcile-background.test.js` exits 0.
5. A full `npm test` run shows no failures attributable to any of the above four files.

## Release Note

No user-visible change: resolved three long-standing test failures seen on every local run.

## Technical Approach

Four largely-independent diagnostics, each starting from the failing assertion's own stated cause:
1. Confirm the currently-installed Impeccable version and coordinate with #2531's resolution (same underlying pin mismatch) rather than re-diagnosing from scratch — pick one fixture-vs-install direction and apply it once.
2. Trace `reconcile()`'s `ALL_CHECKS` registration for the console check under a `pr-first`-configured project — likely a conditional registration gap or a stale fixture assuming a different `integration-model` value than this environment resolves.
3. Trace the stale-PID detection path in the visual-decide `stop` command — likely a `kill -0`/process-existence check whose sandbox behavior differs from the test's assumption (a dead-PID probe that doesn't actually raise `ESRCH` the way the test expects in this environment).
4. Trace why the abandoned-interrupted-run control case in `reconcile-background.test.js` isn't archiving — check whether the archival trigger condition (something keyed off `CLAUDE_TWEAKS_SESSION_ID` being unset) still matches current reconcile-background logic, or whether the logic shifted since #1687 shipped this control case.

### Key Files

- `tests/impeccable-plugin-contract.test.js` — the failing pin-mismatch test (coordinate with #2531)
- `tests/console-execute.test.js` — the failing `ALL_CHECKS` reachability test
- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/reconcile.js` — likely home of the console-check `ALL_CHECKS` registration
- `tests/bin-lib/visual-decide/cli.test.js` — the failing stale-PID test
- `plugin/bin/lib/visual-decide/` — likely home of the `stop` command's PID-liveness check
- `tests/bin-lib/hooks/reconcile-background.test.js` — the failing archival-control test
- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/reconcile-background.js` — likely home of the archival trigger logic (verify actual path before editing)

## Gotchas
- These four failures may have independent root causes and could be split into separate records at `/claude-tweaks:specify` time if that proves cleaner than fixing all four in one build.
- Confirm each fix doesn't regress the "control — unchanged fallback behavior" case reconcile-background.test.js is specifically pinning (#1687 AC2) — that test protects a deliberate behavioral contract, not just incidental passing state.
- #2531 already targets Deliverable 1's exact failure and is `ready` but not yet in flight (no `bot:in-progress`, no open linked PR) — check its status before starting; if it ships first, re-run AC 1 here as verification rather than re-deriving the fix.

groups.body:
Surface: infra

## Current State

OpenAI's own autonomous coding agents reportedly attacked RubyGems.org's supply-chain infrastructure — a vendor's unattended agents causing real infra harm, not a third-party attacker. `dispatch` runs as this user's own unattended agent hub with no documented check on what an autonomous build/dispatch agent is allowed to reach (registries, network egress, credential scope). No existing claude-tweaks check evaluates an agent's blast radius before granting it unattended/`auto:build` trust.

**Verified during shaping:** "blast radius" already appears in this codebase (`dispatch/SKILL.md`, `dispatch/configuration.md`, `dispatch/settle-and-merge.md`, `code-health/SKILL.md`) — but every existing use is the record-scoring sense: how bad a *specific code change* could be if it goes wrong (the `risk:*` label's own "blast radius, reversibility" criteria, `_shared/work-record.md`'s Scoring axis). None of the existing usages audit the *agent's own outer boundary* — what registries, network destinations, or credentials an unattended dispatch/build agent can actually reach, independent of any one task's content. This record's proposal is a genuinely distinct, not-yet-built capability, not a duplicate of the existing risk-scoring mechanism.

## Deliverables

- A hardening check (a lens, or a new row in `/code-health` or `/security-review`) that asks what an autonomous agent's tool/network/credential scope actually is, not just whether a given task behaves correctly — distinct from the existing `risk:*` scoring, which judges a specific change's blast radius, not the agent's standing reach.
- Guidance for scoping dispatch-style unattended agents to least-privilege registry/network access (what should an unattended build agent NOT be able to reach, by default).

## Acceptance Criteria

- The check runs standalone and as a step within `/review` or `/security-review`.
- Applying it to dispatch's own agent-trust config reports pass/fail per scope dimension (registry access, network egress, credential scope — whichever dimensions the implementation settles on).
- `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

Added a hardening check for how much an autonomous agent's tools, network, and credentials can reach.

## Technical Approach

Scope the check's dimensions concretely before implementing — the record names three candidates (registries, network egress, credential scope) but the actual claude-tweaks/dispatch environment (this plugin runs inside Claude Code's own tool sandbox, not a bespoke agent runtime) may only meaningfully audit a subset of these; ground the check in what's actually inspectable/configurable in this environment rather than a generic checklist copied from the source incident's different context (OpenAI's own agent infrastructure is architecturally different from a Claude Code plugin's dispatch mechanism). Integrate as a new check function alongside `/security-review`'s existing checks (the closer thematic fit — credential/scope auditing is security-review's territory) or as a `/code-health` finding category, whichever existing skill's own scan structure fits the "run standalone and as a step within an existing skill" AC most naturally — read both skills' existing check-registration patterns before choosing.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/security-review/` or `plugin/skills/code-health/` — the more likely home for the new check, pending a structural fit decision at build time
- `plugin/skills/dispatch/configuration.md` — dispatch's own agent-trust config, the concrete target the AC's "applying it to dispatch's own config" needs to run against
- `plugin/skills/_shared/work-record.md` — the existing `risk:*` Scoring axis, cited here only to confirm this record's proposal is distinct from it, not to be modified

## Gotchas

- Don't conflate this with the existing `risk:*`/blast-radius record-scoring mechanism — that's per-task judgment already in place; this record's check is about the agent's own standing capability boundary, a different question entirely.
- The source incident (OpenAI agents vs. RubyGems) involved a different agent architecture than this plugin's own dispatch mechanism — treat it as motivating evidence that this class of risk is real, not as a template to copy literally; ground the actual check dimensions in what's true of *this* environment.

## Original request

Add an autonomous-agent blast-radius check to hardening practice

Current State:
- OpenAI's own autonomous coding agents reportedly attacked RubyGems.org's supply-chain infrastructure -- a vendor's unattended agents causing real infra harm, not a third-party attacker.
- dispatch runs as this user's own unattended agent hub with no documented check on what an autonomous build/dispatch agent is allowed to reach (registries, network egress, credential scope).
- No existing claude-tweaks check evaluates an agent's blast radius before granting it unattended/auto:build trust.
Deliverables:
- A hardening check (lens, or a row in /code-health or /security-review) that asks what an autonomous agent's tool/network/credential scope actually is, not just whether it behaves correctly.
- Guidance for scoping dispatch-style unattended agents to least-privilege registry/network access.
Acceptance Criteria:
- The check runs standalone and as a step within /review or /security-review.
- Applying it to dispatch's own agent-trust config reports pass/fail per scope dimension.
Source: https://simonwillison.net/2026/Sep/12/openai-agents-rubygems/

groups.body:
Surface: infra

## Current State

After a merged multi-spec run (`flow/multispec-review-console.md` Shared teardown step 7), `teardown-run --run <archived run> --merged` reported: `worktree: skipped — removal failed`, `branch: skipped — delete failed for <branch>`, `remote ref: skipped — Command failed: gh api --method DELETE repos/<owner>/<repo>/git/refs/heads/<branch>`. Two causes: (1) the `gh api` call carried no host argument, so on a GitHub Enterprise-hosted repo it targeted github.com and failed; (2) the worktree removal had half-reaped the worktree (its `.git` file was gone and `git worktree list` showed `prunable`) but reported failure, and the local branch delete then failed because git still considered the branch checked out there — a `git worktree prune` first would have let both succeed.

Verified during shaping: `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/teardown-run.js`'s `ghApiDelete` helper (line ~30) calls `gh api --method DELETE ...args` with no host/hostname argument, and the branch-delete path (line ~235-236) shows no `git worktree prune` step ahead of it — both causes are confirmed present in the current code, not already fixed. `plugin/bin/lib/repo-resolve.js` exists and is the codebase's own existing mechanism for resolving `host/owner/repo` for a GHE remote — the fix should reuse it rather than inventing new host-resolution logic.

## Deliverables

- Resolve the forge host via `bin/lib/repo-resolve.js` (the existing mechanism) and pass it to every `gh` call `teardown-run` makes, including the `ghApiDelete` helper's `gh api --method DELETE` call — so a GHE-hosted repo's remote-ref deletion targets the correct host instead of defaulting to github.com.
- Before attempting the local branch delete, check whether the worktree removal left the worktree registration in a `prunable` state (`git worktree list` porcelain output) and, if so, run `git worktree prune` first, then retry the branch delete — rather than reporting a failure that a simple prune would have resolved.
- Report all three teardown outcomes (worktree, branch, remote ref) with their underlying error text on failure, not just a generic "skipped" — so a human diagnosing a teardown failure doesn't have to reproduce the command by hand to see the real `gh`/git error.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `teardown-run --merged` against a GitHub Enterprise-hosted repo successfully deletes the remote ref, using the correct host resolved via `repo-resolve.js`.
- A worktree left in a `prunable` state by a partially-successful removal no longer blocks the subsequent branch delete — the prune-then-retry sequence resolves it automatically.
- A teardown failure (any of the three steps) reports the underlying error text in its output, not just "skipped."
- `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

Fixed run teardown on GitHub Enterprise remotes and made it remove the worktree before deleting the branch.

## Technical Approach

Reuse `repo-resolve.js`'s existing host-resolution output directly in `teardown-run.js`'s `gh` invocations (the `ghApiDelete` helper and any other `gh` call site in that file) — this is a straightforward plumbing fix, not new logic, since the resolution mechanism already exists and is used elsewhere in the codebase. For the prune-before-retry fix, check the worktree's state via `git worktree list --porcelain` (or equivalent) immediately after a reported removal failure, and only retry the branch delete after a prune succeeds — don't blindly prune-and-retry on every failure without first confirming the `prunable` state, since a genuinely different failure (e.g. permissions) shouldn't be masked by an unconditional retry.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/teardown-run.js` — `ghApiDelete` (host-resolution fix) and the branch-delete path (prune-before-retry fix)
- `plugin/bin/lib/repo-resolve.js` — the existing host-resolution mechanism to reuse

## Gotchas

- Don't unconditionally retry the branch delete after any failure — only after confirming (via `git worktree list`) that the worktree is genuinely in a `prunable` state; a different underlying cause (e.g. a real permissions error) should still surface as a real failure, not be silently retried into a second, equally-doomed attempt.
- This is a Windows + GHE-specific repro, but the host-resolution fix and the prune-before-retry fix are both platform-independent — verify the fix doesn't regress teardown on a plain github.com-hosted repo (the common case in this repo's own CI).

## Original request

Upstream defect report — `hooks.js teardown-run --merged` cannot finish on a GitHub Enterprise remote and orders the branch delete before the worktree removal

Component: `bin/hooks.js` `teardown-run` (`bin/lib/hooks/teardown-run` / `cleanup-procedures-execution.md` Section C mechanics)
Kind: defect
Version: claude-tweaks 6.126.0, Windows 11, GitHub Enterprise Server host

## Symptom

After a merged multi-spec run (`flow/multispec-review-console.md` Shared teardown step 7), `teardown-run --run <archived run> --merged` reported: `worktree: skipped — removal failed`, `branch: skipped — delete failed for <branch>`, `remote ref: skipped — Command failed: gh api --method DELETE repos/<owner>/<repo>/git/refs/heads/<branch>`. Causes observed: (1) the `gh api` call carried no `GH_HOST`, so on a GHE-hosted repo it targeted github.com and failed; (2) the worktree removal had half-reaped the worktree (its `.git` file was gone and `git worktree list` showed `prunable`) but reported failure, and the local branch delete then failed because git still considered the branch checked out there; a `git worktree prune` first would have let both succeed.

## Expected

Resolve the forge host the way `bin/lib/repo-resolve.js` already does (`host/owner/repo` for a GHE remote) and pass it to every `gh` call in the teardown; on a removal failure whose registration is `prunable`, run `git worktree prune` and retry the branch delete; report the three outcomes with the underlying error text.

## Evidence

djoef/recommender-system run 2026-09-20T195550-spec-497-498-499 close-out, 2026-09-21: the teardown-run output above, followed by the manual recovery (`git worktree prune`, `git branch -D`, `gh api … DELETE` with `GH_HOST` set). Cost: four extra commands.

Surface: infra

## Current State

Three small, related defects from the same session, bundled in one report:

1. `plan-audit.js` Check A flags a plan whose task creates a single new file in a new directory as "lone new file" — the controller had to pre-create empty directories to silence it. Spot-checked during shaping: `plugin/bin/lib/plan-audit/checks.js`'s Check A section has no visible special-case for a new-directory-plus-single-file shape, and this matches a standing workaround already known in this project ("mkdir the new module dir before auditing") — this defect still appears live, not already fixed.
2. On a record materialized with `surface: web` whose diff has no UI trigger file (a loader + route + config record), the pipeline story selection's "web surface → run the full story set" rule fires instead of reading the Layer 3 sniff first — wasting a full QA pass on a non-UI diff.
3. `node --test "<abs file>"` on Windows globs a path containing `[id]` (a Next.js dynamic-segment directory) and finds no test; the single-file invocation had to go through `tsx --test` with a quoted path as a workaround.

## Deliverables

- [ ] `plan-audit.js` Check A: count a new directory's files together, or explicitly accept a task whose only change is creating a new directory plus one file within it, rather than flagging the single file as a "lone new file" false positive.
- [ ] `/test`'s pipeline story selection: read the Layer 3 frontend-detection sniff (the same one Surface: web/mobile/desktop/backend/infra resolution already uses elsewhere) before defaulting a `surface: web` record with no UI trigger file to the full story set — a web-surface record whose actual diff carries no UI signal should not automatically run every QA story.
- [ ] `skills/test/verification.md`'s single-file test invocation: document (or escape) bracketed path segments (e.g. Next.js `[id]` dynamic-segment directories) so `node --test` globbing doesn't silently find zero tests on Windows — either a documented escaping convention or a fallback invocation path (the filer's own workaround used `tsx --test` with a quoted path).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A plan task that creates exactly one new file inside a newly-created directory passes Check A without requiring the directory to be pre-created empty.
2. A `surface: web` record whose diff has no UI trigger file does not automatically run the full QA story set — the Layer 3 sniff's result is consulted first.
3. A single-file `node --test` invocation against a path containing a bracketed segment (`[id]`-style) finds and runs its test correctly on Windows, or `verification.md` documents the required escaping/fallback clearly enough that a controller doesn't have to rediscover the `tsx --test` workaround independently.
4. `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

Fixed plan audit false positives on new directories, full QA running on non-UI changes, and test globs with brackets.

## Technical Approach

Three independent, small fixes sharing no code path — safe to land as one record (small, related, same session's evidence) or split at build time if that reads cleaner, but nothing here requires sequencing. (1) is a Check A classification-logic fix in `plan-audit/checks.js`. (2) reuses the existing Layer 3 sniff mechanism (`design-wrapper/frontend-detection.md`'s Layer 2/3 signal, already used elsewhere per root CLAUDE.md's Auto-Mode Contract citation) rather than inventing new detection logic — call the existing sniff from the story-selection rule instead of defaulting past it. (3) is either a doc fix (state the escaping convention) or a small invocation-path change in `verification.md`'s single-file test command — prefer the doc fix first, since introducing a `tsx` dependency for this narrow case is a bigger footprint than documenting the existing workaround clearly.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/plan-audit/checks.js` — Check A's new-file/new-directory classification logic
- `plugin/skills/test/SKILL.md` — the pipeline story selection rule defaulting to the full set on `surface: web`
- `plugin/skills/design-wrapper/frontend-detection.md` — the existing Layer 2/3 sniff mechanism the story-selection rule should consult
- `plugin/skills/test/verification.md` — the single-file test invocation needing the bracket-path documentation/fix

## Gotchas

- Don't let (2)'s fix silently skip QA on a record that genuinely does need the full story set — the Layer 3 sniff should inform the decision, not replace human/build judgment entirely; a record with an ambiguous or borderline diff should still default toward running stories, not skipping them, per this project's general caution-toward-more-checking posture.
- (3) is Windows-specific (the filer's evidence names Windows explicitly) — verify the fix doesn't change behavior on macOS/Linux where the bracket-globbing issue may not reproduce the same way.
